classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: silane_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous injection rate of silane (SiH4) gas into the plasma vessel,
expressed as an electron-equivalent particle rate with 18 equivalent
electrons for each SiH4 molecule.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of silane ($\mathrm{SiH}_4$) gas into the
plasma vessel is the silane gas source rate expressed on an
electron-equivalent particle-counting basis. Each $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule
contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to the total electron count of a
neutral molecule.

The conversion from a molecular silane injection rate to this
electron-equivalent source rate is

$$
S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the silane source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ is the molecular injection rate of neutral silane
into the plasma vessel, and 18 is the electron-equivalent count of one
neutral $\mathrm{SiH}_4$ molecule.

This quantity applies only to silane gas introduced into the plasma vessel
and is aggregated over all silane introduced into that vessel on the same
electron-equivalent basis. It excludes source rates for other gasses, total
gas-source rates, silicon-only or hydrogen-only atomic source rates, mass
flow, neutral-gas inventory, and pressure.

The silane source count is the time integral of $S_{\mathrm{SiH}_4}$ using
the same factor of 18 between molecular count and electron-equivalent count.
This quantity is the silane analog of the [ethylene source
rate](name:ethylene_source_rate) and [ethane source
rate](name:ethane_source_rate); the molecular identity fixes the conversion
factor in each case.

Sign convention: Positive when silane is added to the plasma vessel.

items.name: electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption
items.description:
Exponential e-folding time for the electron-temperature decrease at the
magnetic axis during a disruption.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the characteristic e-folding time of the electron
temperature at the magnetic axis during a disruption. It describes
exponential temperature loss and is distinct from the [linear electron decay
time at the magnetic
axis](name:linear_electron_decay_time_at_magnetic_axis_due_to_disruption),
which uses a 20–80% definition.

For an exponential decay beginning at reference time $t_0$, the temperature
is represented by:

$$
T_e(t)=T_{e,0}\exp\left[-\frac{t-t_0}{\tau}\right]
$$

where $T_e(t)$ is the electron temperature at time $t$, $T_{e,0}$ is its
value at the reference time $t_0$, and $\tau$ is the decay time constant.
The quantity applies specifically to the magnetic-axis temperature and the
disruption-related decay; it is not a volume-averaged or runaway-electron
decay time.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface, formed from the corresponding volume-averaged
densities. The argon population is summed over all argon ion charge states
and excludes neutral argon.
items.documentation:
Elemental abundance ratio of argon nuclei to free electrons inside the last
closed flux surface is the confined-plasma composition fraction obtained by
normalizing the volume-averaged argon density to the volume-averaged
electron density. The argon population is the species-level ion population
summed over all argon ion charge states.

The ratio is defined as the quotient of the corresponding volume-averaged
densities:

$$
C_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V}{\langle n_e\rangle_V}
$$

where $C_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is this argon-to-electron abundance ratio, $\langle
n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged argon-ion number
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged electron number
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and $V$ denotes the
confined plasma volume bounded by the last closed flux surface.

The scope is the confined plasma population inside the last closed flux
surface, with the same volume-averaging operation applied to the argon and
electron densities before forming the quotient. It excludes neutral argon,
is not charge-state-resolved, and is a ratio of volume averages rather than
the volume average of a local argon-to-electron density ratio.

This quantity is related to [argon_density](name:argon_density) as its
volume-averaged, electron-normalized elemental abundance;
[argon_density](name:argon_density) denotes the argon density before
normalization to the electron population.

items.name: upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient measuring how the upper outboard
(low-field-side) corner of the plasma boundary departs from the reference
ellipse defined by boundary minor radius, upper elongation, and upper
triangularity.
items.documentation:
The upper outer squareness $\zeta_{uo}$ is one of four corner-specific shape
parameters in the Luce (2013) plasma boundary parameterization, describing
how much the upper outer quadrant of the plasma cross-section boundary
deviates from the reference ellipse defined by the boundary minor radius
$a$, upper elongation $\kappa_u$, and upper triangularity $\delta_u$. In the
poloidal cross-section expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height, this
quadrant is the large-$R$, larger-$Z$ corner relative to the boundary shape
center.

With poloidal parameter $\theta$ increasing from the outboard midplane point
to the top point, the upper-outboard Luce boundary segment is parameterized
by

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(\theta) &= R_0 + a\cos\left[\theta + \arcsin(\delta_u)\sin\theta - \zeta_{uo}\sin(2\theta)\right],\\
Z(\theta) &= Z_0 + \kappa_u a\sin\left[\theta + \zeta_{uo}\sin(2\theta)\right],\quad 0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

where $(R(\theta), Z(\theta))$ is the boundary point in the poloidal
cross-section, $R_0$ and $Z_0$ are the shape-center coordinates, $a$ is the
boundary minor radius, $\kappa_u$ is the upper elongation, and $\delta_u$ is
the upper triangularity.

The value $\zeta_{uo}=0$ is the reference-ellipse case for the
upper-outboard quadrant after $a$, $\kappa_u$, and $\delta_u$ have been
fixed; nonzero values describe residual corner shaping rather than minor
radius, elongation, or triangularity. Together with
[lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
[upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
and
[lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
it forms the four-corner boundary squareness decomposition;
[outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
combines the two outboard corner contributions, while
[squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) is the
single-coefficient boundary summary.

Sign convention: Positive when the upper outer boundary corner lies outside
the reference ellipse at the same poloidal parameter, i.e., toward larger
$R$ and larger $Z$ relative to the shape center in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height.

items.name: saturated_ion_current_density
items.description:
Conventional ion charge flux per collecting area at a Langmuir-probe
collector in the negative-bias saturation regime, where electron collection
is suppressed.
items.documentation:
The saturated ion current density is the limiting conventional ion
charge-flux density reaching a Langmuir-probe collector biased sufficiently
negative relative to the plasma to suppress electron collection. It is the
ion-saturation specialization of [ion current
density](name:ion_current_density), rather than the unrestricted [current
density](name:current_density) carried by all charged particles.

The charge-weighted ion flux defines the current-density vector:

$$
\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}} = \sum_a \sum_{z\geq 1} z e\,\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the saturated ion current-density
vector, $i$ denotes the ion population, $a$ labels ion species, $z$ is the
positive ionic charge number, $e$ is the elementary charge, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{a,z}^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is the particle-flux vector of
that species and charge state at the collector in ion saturation.

The sum includes all collected ion species and charge states, weighted by
their electric charge. Electron and neutral-particle contributions are
excluded. This is a charge flux per collecting area, not an area-integrated
current or an unweighted ion particle flux.

The [saturated ion current](name:saturated_ion_current) is the surface
integral of the collector-directed component:
$I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}=\int_S\mathbf{j}_{i,\mathrm{sat}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}\,dA$,
where $I_{i,\mathrm{sat}}$ is the collected saturated ion current, $S$ is
the collecting surface, $dA$ is a surface-area element, and
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{col}}$ is the unit normal directed from the
plasma into the collector. The [fluctuating saturated ion current
density](name:fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density) is the temporal
standard deviation of the collected current-density component; no temporal
statistical operation is implied here.

Sign convention: Positive when positive ion charge flows from the plasma
into the collector, as defined by the collector-directed normal.

items.name: plasma_momentum_flux
items.description:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface, summed over charged plasma populations and excluding neutral
transport.
items.documentation:
The plasma momentum flux describes the rate at which charged plasma
populations transport linear momentum through a unit area of an oriented
surface. It includes convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions.

$$
\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{charged}}\left(\rho_s\mathbf{v}_s\mathbf{v}_s + p_s\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}_s\right)
$$

Here, $\mathbf{F}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the momentum-flux vector,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the charged-plasma momentum-flux tensor,
and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the oriented unit surface normal. The sum covers
charged species $s$; $\rho_s$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ bulk velocity,
$p_s$ scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}_s$ the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This charged-plasma specialization belongs to the broader [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux) family and excludes the neutral contribution
represented by [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux). Its
field-aligned projection is [parallel plasma momentum
flux](name:parallel_plasma_momentum_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when momentum transport across the surface is
directed along the chosen surface normal.

items.name: inner_radius_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Non-negative radial distance from the toroidal symmetry axis to the inner
boundary of an annular iron-core segment. Together with the outer radius, it
fixes the radial extent of the hollow cross section.
items.documentation:
The inner radius of an iron-core segment is the non-negative major-radius
distance from the toroidal symmetry axis to the inner boundary of an annular
iron region. It is expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

For an annular cross-section, the inner radius $R_{\rm in}$ is the radial
location of the inner boundary, and it is smaller than the corresponding
outer radius $R_{\rm out}$:

$$
0 \le R_{\rm in} < R_{\rm out}
$$

The quantity specifies the hollow-bore boundary and radial extent, not the
position along the toroidal direction, vertical height, boundary thickness,
or local curvature of an arc. Unlike the curvature radius represented by
radius of an iron-core segment, it is a radial boundary dimension. Together
with the [outer radius of an iron-core
segment](name:outer_radius_of_iron_core_segment), it defines the annular
radial interval.

items.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part
items.description:
Signed in-phase quadrature of the right-hand circular E-minus wave
electric-field phasor, transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field
and defined relative to a chosen phase reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed in-phase quadrature of the right-hand circularly
polarized wave electric-field phasor, transverse to the local equilibrium
magnetic field. It describes the E-minus contribution to local wave
polarization along a beam or ray path.

Its defining relation is

$$
E_{-,r} = \operatorname{Re}(\widetilde{E}_{-})
$$

where $E_{-,r}$ is the real quadrature defined here, $\widetilde{E}_{-}$ is
the [right-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field
phasor](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and
$\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real-part operator relative to the chosen
phase reference.

The quantity applies locally along the propagation path, including
electron-cyclotron-emission beam or ray paths; it is not integrated or
averaged along that path. It is distinct from the phasor modulus and from
the instantaneous physical electric field.

Together with the [imaginary
quadrature](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part),
denoted $E_{-,i}$, it reconstructs the parent phasor through
$\widetilde{E}_{-}=E_{-,r}+iE_{-,i}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit. Both
quadratures must use the same polarization basis and phase reference. The
[left-hand real
quadrature](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part)
instead resolves the E-plus polarization contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-minus phase differs from the chosen
zero-phase reference by less than a quarter-cycle, modulo a full cycle.

items.name: iron_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the particle
count per volume for iron ions at the sheath entrance immediately upstream
of the target-facing plasma boundary. Positive charge states are summed;
neutral iron is excluded.
items.documentation:
Number density of the iron species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the iron-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local iron-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $\mathrm{Fe}$
denotes iron, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of free iron ions, and $V$ is
a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the
plasma side.

This quantity applies to the free iron-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive iron charge states,
counting each iron ion once without charge-state weighting. Neutral iron
atoms, electrons, other ion species, and charge density are excluded.

It is a species-resolved component of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target), whereas
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target)
describes the free-electron population and
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target)
applies the same target-locus and charge-state-summed convention to carbon
ions.

items.name: wave_frequency
items.description:
Temporal carrier frequency of a coherent electromagnetic wave used to
characterize its oscillation rate in plasma heating and current drive.
items.documentation:
Wave frequency is the non-negative temporal carrier frequency of a coherent
electromagnetic wave interacting with a plasma. It describes the rate of
phase oscillation and applies to waves at launch or during propagation,
independent of the wave amplitude or absorbed power.

The frequency $f$ is related to the angular frequency by

$$
f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}
$$

where $f$ is frequency in hertz and $\omega$ is angular frequency in radians
per second. The launch-specific quantity launched wave frequency uses this
same definition as the absolute reference for a launched wave, while
[frequency of electron cyclotron heating
antenna](name:frequency_of_electron_cyclotron_beam) is a device-specific
instance.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Effective toroidal fluid velocity of a neutral species occupying a specified
internal quantum state, retaining only the contribution attributed to
diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation:
The effective neutral internal-state diamagnetic drift velocity is the
fluid-level velocity of a neutral species population occupying a defined
internal quantum state, restricted here to its toroidal component and
diamagnetic contribution. This component is derived from the parent
effective neutral internal-state diamagnetic drift velocity and is distinct
from the corresponding state-aggregated [toroidal neutral-state diamagnetic
drift
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the effective neutral internal-state
diamagnetic drift velocity and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal
unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_velocity_of_pellet
items.description:
Signed vertical component of the pellet center-of-mass velocity, parallel to
the symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed vertical component of the translational velocity
of the pellet center of mass. It resolves motion in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical velocity is defined by:

$$
v_Z = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{dZ_{\mathrm{cm}}}{dt}
$$

where $v_Z$ is the vertical velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$
is the pellet center-of-mass velocity vector, $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit
vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$, $Z_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is
the vertical coordinate of the pellet center of mass, and $t$ is time.

For a shattered pellet, this quantity describes the mass-weighted bulk
motion of the fragment cloud, not an individual fragment's velocity. It
excludes rotational motion about the center of mass and is not restricted to
the initial value at vacuum-chamber entry.

Together with the [radial velocity of the
pellet](name:radial_velocity_of_pellet) and [toroidal velocity of the
pellet](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet), it specifies the translational
velocity vector when all components refer to the same pellet and instant.
This signed component is distinct from the speed, which is the magnitude of
that vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the pellet center of mass moves toward
increasing $Z$.

items.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density produced by diamagnetic drift in a
magnetized plasma, representing the signed field-aligned return current that
cancels the divergence of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic current.
items.documentation:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
field-aligned scalar return current associated with the
pressure-gradient-driven current described by
[current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).
It enforces charge-current continuity by canceling the divergence of the
perpendicular diamagnetic current on a magnetic flux surface in toroidal
geometry.

The scalar amplitude $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is defined by the
current-continuity condition

$$
\nabla \cdot \left(j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}\mathbf{b}\right) = -\nabla \cdot \left(\frac{\mathbf{B} \times \nabla p}{B^2}\right)
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{PS,dia}}$ is the signed scalar Pfirsch-Schlueter current
density due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit
vector along the magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field,
$B^2=\mathbf{B}\cdot\mathbf{B}$, and $p$ is the isotropic scalar plasma
pressure.

This scalar denotes the amplitude multiplying the magnetic-field unit
vector, not an independent vector current and not a cylindrical component. A
flux-surface-constant parallel current component not required by the
diamagnetic-current divergence is excluded; the component-oriented
[parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
denotes the parallel projection of the same field-aligned contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional positive charge flows along the
local magnetic field direction $\mathbf{B}$.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Imaginary part of the complex toroidal component of the first-order
magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region,
for a specified toroidal mode number in linear MHD stability analysis.
items.documentation:
In linear MHD stability analysis for a specified toroidal mode number $n$,
the first-order magnetic-field perturbation $\delta\mathbf{B}$ in the
current-free vacuum region surrounding the plasma is a complex eigenfunction
satisfying $\nabla \times \delta\mathbf{B} = 0$ and $\nabla \cdot
\delta\mathbf{B} = 0$. This name gives the imaginary part of the toroidal
projection of that eigenfunction:

$$
\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac} = \delta\mathbf{B}^\mathrm{vac} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
so that $\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac} = \mathrm{Re}(\delta
B_\phi^\mathrm{vac}) + i\,\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac})$.

The real part is given by
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part),
and together they constitute the parent complex eigenfunction
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field).
Boundary conditions at the plasma–vacuum interface link this vacuum
eigenfunction to the corresponding plasma-region toroidal component
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part);
the radial vacuum counterpart is
[radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part).
Absolute eigenfunction amplitudes are normalization-convention-dependent in
linear stability calculations.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathrm{Im}(\delta B_\phi^\mathrm{vac})$ is
directed in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: pedestal_thermal_ion_energy
items.description:
Volume-integrated random kinetic energy of thermal ions within the H-mode
edge pedestal, excluding electron energy, bulk-flow energy, and nonthermal
ion contributions.
items.documentation:
Pedestal thermal ion energy is the internal energy stored by thermal-ion
populations within the H-mode edge pedestal. It is the pedestal-region
contribution to [thermal ion energy](name:thermal_ion_energy), rather than
the energy of the entire confined ion population.

For isotropic, nonrelativistic thermal ions, the defining relation is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{ped},i} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{ped}}} p_{\mathrm{th},i}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{ped},i}$ is the pedestal thermal ion energy,
$V_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the pedestal integration region, $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$
is the thermal-ion pressure summed over all included ion species and
positive charge states, and $dV$ is a differential physical volume element.

The quantity is a volume-integrated energy content, not the local [ion
average temperature at the pedestal
top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top). It excludes directed
bulk-flow energy, fast-ion and other suprathermal contributions, and
electron energy. The separate [pedestal thermal electron
energy](name:pedestal_thermal_electron_energy) supplies the electron
contribution; their sum gives the combined ion–electron thermal energy for
the same pedestal region.

items.name: vertical_plasma_velocity
items.description:
Vertical component of the bulk plasma center-of-mass velocity along the Z
direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, representing
vertical mass transport of all contributing plasma species.
items.documentation:
The vertical plasma velocity is the projection of the bulk [plasma
velocity](name:plasma_velocity) onto the vertical basis direction $\hat{Z}$
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis is
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. It represents the mass-weighted
center-of-mass flow of all contributing plasma species in the vertical
direction.

The projected component is defined by:

$$
v_Z = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{plasma} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $v_Z$ is the vertical plasma velocity, $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{plasma}$ is
the bulk [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity), and $\hat{Z}$ is the
vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the bulk plasma mixture wherever a local fluid
center-of-mass velocity is defined. It uses the same aggregation convention
as the parent plasma velocity: species velocities are weighted by mass
density and combined over all contributing plasma species. It is a scalar
cylindrical projection, not the full velocity vector, not a vertical
position or displacement, and not a species-resolved velocity.

Together with the [radial plasma velocity](name:radial_plasma_velocity) and
the [toroidal center-of-mass
velocity](name:toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity), it forms the cylindrical
component decomposition of the bulk [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity).
The [parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity) is a separate
projection onto the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$ and is not
generally identical to the vertical component.

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma center-of-mass velocity has a
component in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction, toward increasing vertical coordinate
$Z$.

items.name: current_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Current of a toroidal-field coil is the signed conventional electric current
carried by one toroidal-field-coil winding. Its sign is defined by the
toroidal magnetic-field component produced by that coil.
items.documentation:
Current of a toroidal-field coil is the signed conventional electric current
carried by one toroidal-field-coil winding. It represents the coil current
that sources that coil's contribution to the toroidal magnetic field.

The signed current is the current-density flux through an oriented
cross-section of the winding conductor:

$$
I = \int_S \mathbf{J} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $I$ is the coil current, $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional current
density, $S$ is the oriented cross-section, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is its unit
normal, and $dA$ is the surface area element.

This quantity is an individual coil or coil-circuit current. It excludes
multiplication by the number of turns, summation over a toroidal-field-coil
set, and currents induced in passive conducting structures such as [current
of passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure). It is distinct
from terminal [voltage of a toroidal-field
coil](name:voltage_of_toroidal_field_coil) and from [resistance of a
toroidal-field coil](name:resistance_of_toroidal_field_coil).

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal component of the magnetic-field
contribution from the coil is positive, $B_\phi > 0$, in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description:
Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the signed coefficient
multiplying one ion species’ toroidal momentum, with negative values
describing proportional damping.
items.documentation:
Toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate is the coefficient of the
proportional source contribution treated implicitly in an ion species’
toroidal momentum equation. It is the toroidal specialization of [implicit
ion momentum source rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate), rather
than a dimensional momentum source.

Its defining relation is:

$$
\left(\frac{\partial P_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{imp}} = S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}} P_{i,\phi}
$$

where $P_{i,\phi}$ is the primary toroidal [momentum](name:momentum)
quantity for ion species $i$, $t$ is time, $S_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is
this source coefficient, and the label $\mathrm{imp}$ identifies the
implicitly treated source contribution. The toroidal direction is the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The coefficient applies to one specified ion species, with the primary
momentum summed over that species’ ionic charge states. It is neither summed
over all ion species nor explicitly charge-state resolved; the coefficient
itself is not a sum of charge-state coefficients.

Unlike a positive [momentum damping rate](name:momentum_damping_rate), this
signed coefficient can describe either proportional amplification or
damping. It excludes the additive source contribution independent of the
primary momentum and is not a volume-integrated torque such as [toroidal
explicit ion torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque).

Sign convention: Positive when the implicit source contribution reinforces
the existing toroidal momentum; negative when it opposes that momentum and
damps its magnitude.

items.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of iron impurity ions evaluated
at the last closed flux surface in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the bulk-flow velocity of
iron impurity ions at the last closed flux surface. The iron bulk-flow
velocity is the density-weighted mean over all included iron ionization
states.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the projection is
defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the toroidal velocity component,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The value is local to the plasma boundary and is distinct from the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal iron velocity, which averages the same
projection over that surface. It is the iron-species counterpart of
[toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the iron bulk-flow velocity has a component
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: effective_particle_energy
items.description:
Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic kinetic-energy-like coordinate
that orders a species in velocity space and may be scaled by a positive
reference energy.
items.documentation:
Effective particle energy is a gyrokinetic velocity-space energy assigned to
a particle species through a kinetic-energy-like weight. It provides the
energy coordinate used to order that species in velocity space and is the
unnormalized concept underlying [normalized effective particle
energy](name:normalized_effective_particle_energy). It differs from
[particle energy](name:particle_energy), which denotes the energy content of
the full distribution.

The effective energy is defined by the selected velocity-space weight:

$$
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}(\boldsymbol{\xi}) = w_s(\boldsymbol{\xi})
$$

where $s$ labels the species, $\boldsymbol{\xi}$ denotes its velocity-space
variables, and $w_s$ is a kinetic-energy-like weight, such as the total
kinetic energy or a directional component. A normalized specialization
divides $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{eff},s}$ by a strictly positive species
reference energy. This quantity is distinct from perturbed particle energy,
which describes a moment of a distribution perturbation rather than the
effective energy coordinate itself.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Mass-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of the effective deuterium–tritium
fuel species evaluated at the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity assigned to
deuterium–tritium fuel treated as one effective species at the radial
location of the internal transport barrier. It describes collective fuel
motion rather than the velocity of an individual isotope or charge state.

The component is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the effective deuterium–tritium bulk
velocity and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [toroidal deuterium velocity at
the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
this quantity represents the effective deuterium–tritium fuel species.

Sign convention: Positive when $V_{\phi,\mathrm{DT}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the density-weighted bulk velocity of tungsten
impurity ions at the last closed flux surface separating confined plasma
from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal projection of the tungsten impurity-ion
bulk velocity at the plasma boundary, defined on the last closed flux
surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer. It is a
density-weighted mean over the included tungsten ion charge states.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{W}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)=\\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\left[\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)\\cdot\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}\\right]}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}(\\mathbf{x}_b)}
$$

Here, $q$ is the tungsten ion charge state, $n_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its
number density, $\\mathbf{v}_{\\mathrm{W}^{q+}}$ is its bulk velocity,
$\\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the boundary, and $\\hat{\\boldsymbol{\\phi}}$
is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$
frame. Unlike
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary, this
quantity is local rather than flux-surface averaged.

Sign convention: Positive when the tungsten-ion velocity component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

items.name: z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Signed z-component of the shatter-cone major-axis unit vector, specifying
its orientation along z in the right-handed Cartesian frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed projection of the shatter-cone major-axis unit
vector onto the Cartesian z direction. It specifies the major-axis
orientation along z, not an axis length or a position coordinate.

The component is defined by

$$
u_{\mathrm{major},z} = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}} \cdot \hat{z}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the unit vector along the
shatter-cone major axis and $\hat{z}$ is the z basis vector in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ frame. Together with the
[x major-axis unit-vector
component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [y major-axis
unit-vector component](name:y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), it
defines the Cartesian orientation of that axis. It is distinct from the [z
minor-axis unit-vector
component](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone).

items.name: ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by all ion populations — thermal and fast —
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The ion power at inside flux surface is the cumulative rate at which wave
energy is deposited into the ion population — spanning both thermal bulk
ions and fast (non-thermal) ions — within the plasma volume bounded by a
closed magnetic flux surface. It is the ion-channel component of the more
general [power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separating ion energy absorption from the corresponding electron heating
contribution.

The quantity is the volume integral of the total ion wave-power density
$p_i(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\psi)$ enclosed by the flux
surface labeled $\psi$:

$$
P_i(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_i(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_i$ is the ion volumetric heating power density in W m$^{-3}$ and
$\psi$ is the chosen flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal
flux radius $\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

The population-resolved breakdown is given by
[thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
for the bulk ion channel and
[fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
for non-thermal beam or fusion-born ions. This cumulative radial profile
enables power-balance analysis and is inferred from combining absorbed-power
density profiles computed via wave ray-tracing or Monte Carlo
beam-deposition codes with equilibrium flux-surface geometry.

items.name: neon_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel, expressed
as an equivalent-electron count rate with ten counts assigned to each
injected neon atom.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel is the time
rate of increase of the equivalent-electron count associated with injected
neon. The equivalent-electron convention assigns ten counts to each injected
neon atom, reflecting neon's atomic number.

The defining relation to injected atom count is:

$$
S_\mathrm{Ne} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}}{dt} = 10\,\frac{dN_\mathrm{Ne}}{dt}
$$

where $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the neon source rate,
$N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^\mathrm{Ne}$ is the equivalent-electron count assigned to
injected neon, $N_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the count of injected neon atoms, $t$ is
time, and the label $\mathrm{Ne}$ denotes neon.

This quantity is species-specific to neon gas entering the plasma vessel and
is aggregated over the injected neon population by summing the
equivalent-electron contributions from all injected neon atoms. It excludes
injection of other gasses, total gas throughput, pumping or exhaust flow,
retained neutral inventory, and source terms from wall recycling,
sputtering, or ionization inside the plasma.

The corresponding [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count) is
the time integral of $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ over the accumulation interval using
the same factor of ten. Conversely, where differentiable, $S_\mathrm{Ne}$ is
the time derivative of that accumulated count.

Sign convention: Positive when neon is added to the plasma vessel.

items.name: hot_neutral_fraction
items.description:
Dimensionless fraction of the hot charge-exchange-born component of a
hydrogen-isotope neutral population relative to the total neutral atom
population.
items.documentation:
The hot neutral fraction is a dimensionless ratio bounded in $[0, 1]$
expressing the relative abundance of the hot, charge-exchange-born component
of a hydrogen-isotope neutral population. It is a component of the broader
[neutral
fraction](name:ratio_of_neutral_state_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density),
distinct from the cold recycled component.

The fraction is defined as:

$$
f_{\mathrm{hot}} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{hot}}}{n_{\mathrm{cold}} + n_{\mathrm{hot}}}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{hot}}$ is the hot neutral fraction, $n_{\mathrm{hot}}$ is
the number density of hot charge-exchange-born neutral atoms, and
$n_{\mathrm{cold}}$ is the number density of cold recycled neutral atoms.

The quantity applies to a specified hydrogen isotope and uses the
two-component neutral-population model. Its denominator is the total neutral
population formed by the cold and hot components for that isotope; it is not
summed across different isotopes and does not represent the cold component
itself.

Within this model, the hot and cold fractions are complementary and sum to
unity. The [cold neutral fraction](name:cold_neutral_fraction) gives the
corresponding recycled component, with the energy threshold separating the
two components defined by the applicable population model.

items.name: outer_radius_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Outer radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the outer
circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a
current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the external boundary of the
conducting annular region.
items.documentation:
Outer radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the outer
circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a
current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the external boundary of the
conducting annular region; material outside this boundary is not part of
that annular filament cross-section.

For the outer circular boundary in the poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the outer radius
$r_\mathrm{outer}$ is the distance from the filament cross-section center
$(R_c, Z_c)$ to any point $(R, Z)$ on that boundary:

$$
r_\mathrm{outer} = \sqrt{(R - R_c)^2 + (Z - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height,
$(R_c, Z_c)$ is the center of the annular cross-section, and $(R, Z)$ lies
on the outer circular boundary.

The quantity applies only to the outer boundary of an annular
plasma-filament cross-section and is a single geometric radius for that
boundary, not an average over the conducting region. It is the outer member
of radius of a plasma filament, paired with the [inner
radius](name:inner_radius_of_plasma_filament) $r_\mathrm{inner}$; by
definition $0 \le r_\mathrm{inner} \le r_\mathrm{outer}$, and the
current-carrying cross-section occupies the annular region between the two
radii. For the same annular geometry, the area of a plasma filament $A$
satisfies $A = \pi(r_\mathrm{outer}^2 - r_\mathrm{inner}^2)$, where $A$ is
the area of the annular plasma-filament cross-section and $\pi$ is the
circle constant. This quantity excludes the major radius of the filament
center about the toroidal symmetry axis and rectangular cross-section
dimensions such as [plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) and
[height of a plasma filament](name:height_of_plasma_filament).

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of carbon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface at the plasma boundary, summed over all carbon ion charge states and
excluding neutral carbon.
items.documentation:
Number density of carbon

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{C}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{C}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{C}}\rangle$ is the averaged carbon-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the local carbon-ion number density, $S$ is the
flux surface at the specified plasma-boundary locus, $dS$ is its surface
element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude
provides the weighting.

This quantity is summed over all carbon ion charge states and excludes
neutral carbon. It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point
value, a charge-state-resolved density, or a volume average. The
transformation from the local [carbon-ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary) replaces the pointwise
value with the inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. It is
the carbon-specific counterpart of [flux-surface-averaged neon density at
the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: x_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
items.description:
Signed x coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture,
measured from the origin of its right-handed camera Cartesian (x, y, z)
frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity locates the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture along
the x axis of its right-handed camera Cartesian basis
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$. It is a signed geometric position, not an
aperture dimension or orientation.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
x_A = (\mathbf{r}_A - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{x}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_A$ is the position of the aperture center, $\mathbf{r}_0$
is the frame origin, $\hat{x}$ is the unit vector along the x axis, and
$x_A$ is measured in m. The corresponding [y coordinate of the diagnostic
aperture](name:y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture) uses the same origin and
camera basis; this quantity is distinct from cylindrical radial and vertical
aperture coordinates.

Sign convention: Positive when the aperture center lies in the direction of
increasing x from the frame origin.

items.name: turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Signed count of complete winding turns in a poloidal magnetic-field probe
coil, fixing the orientation and magnitude of its magnetic-flux linkage.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed number of complete winding turns in a poloidal
magnetic-field probe coil. Its magnitude counts the turns, while its sign
records the winding orientation used to define magnetic-flux linkage.

For turns with a common flux orientation, the total flux linkage is

$$
\Lambda = N\Phi_1
$$

where $\Lambda$ is the total magnetic flux linkage of the coil, $N$ is the
signed winding-turn count, and $\Phi_1$ is the magnetic flux through one
turn using the probe's reference orientation.

This quantity applies to one physical poloidal magnetic-field probe coil and
aggregates all of its complete winding turns, assigning one signed
contribution to each turn. It is a literal coil-turn count, not the local
poloidal magnetic-field value and not the geometric area enclosed by a turn.

For this probe, the literal winding count provides the physical
specialization of the equivalent coupling count represented by
[effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop);
unlike that broader quantity, it is not a homogenized or equivalent
passive-loop count that may be fractional. Together with the
[area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe),
it determines the probe's per-turn magnetic-flux coupling. The corresponding
toroidal-coil quantity is
[turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe).

items.name: neon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the
last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization stages.
items.documentation:
Number density of neon ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle
count per physical volume for the neon-ion population evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The population is summed over all ionization
stages from singly ionized neon, Ne$^+$, through fully stripped neon,
Ne$^{10+}$.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b)=\int f_{\mathrm{Ne}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a
point on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the velocity distribution function aggregated over the
included neon ion charge states, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space
volume element.

The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called
the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off layer. This quantity is evaluated locally at that boundary and is
not averaged over the flux surface. It includes neon ions across all charge
states from Ne$^+$ through Ne$^{10+}$ and excludes neutral neon and other
particle species.

This quantity is the neon-specific specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). It is
distinct from flux_surface_averaged_neon_density_at_plasma_boundary, which
applies the same charge-state aggregation to a flux-surface average rather
than a local boundary value.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate locating the center of a poloidal magnetic-field
probe in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the major-radius
location of the probe center relative to the toroidal symmetry axis,
expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, c6, Z)$ frame.

The coordinate is defined by the magnitude of the displacement perpendicular
to the toroidal symmetry axis:

$$
R = \left|\mathbf{r}_{\perp}\right|
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate and $\mathbf{r}_{\perp}$ is the
displacement from the toroidal symmetry axis within the plane perpendicular
to that axis.

This quantity applies specifically to the geometric center of one poloidal
magnetic-field probe and is not an aggregate over multiple probes or a
coordinate of the measured magnetic field. It identifies the radial location
only; the corresponding vertical location is given by the [vertical
coordinate of the poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:vertical_coordinate_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe).

It is the probe-specific specialization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that coordinate
at the probe center.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel pseudo-species in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, equal to the
sum of the local deuterium and tritium ion densities.
items.documentation:
Deuterium-tritium density at the limiter is the local number density of the
combined DT fuel ion pseudo-species in the boundary plasma immediately
adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of
the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The DT pseudo-species represents
deuterium and tritium ions as a single fictitious fuel constituent with an
effective per-ion mass of $\bar{m} \approx 2.5\,m_u$ (where $m_u$ is the
unified atomic mass unit) for an equimolar D-T mixture.

The quantity equals the sum of the separate deuterium and tritium ion
densities at the limiter contact point:

$$
n_{DT} = n_D + n_T
$$

where $n_D$ is the local deuterium ion number density and $n_T$ is the local
tritium ion number density at the same evaluation point.

This quantity is the limiter-contact analog of
[deuterium_tritium_density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) and the DT-fuel
counterpart of
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter) at the
same locus. It differs from
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary)
in evaluation geometry: the limiter contact lies in the scrape-off layer on
open field lines, not at the last-closed flux surface. As a member of the
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent family, the presheath
evaluation convention and locus definition follow those of
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) and other
sibling fuel-species densities.

items.name: toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Toroidal width of the antenna strap is its full edge-to-edge physical extent
in the direction around the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Width of antenna strap

The width $w_\phi$ follows the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance
from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical position. It is a non-negative
geometric length, not an angular span or a signed vector component.

The quantity applies to an individual strap and denotes its full width, not
a half-width or the combined span of multiple straps. It is distinct from
the [height of the antenna strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), which
describes its vertical extent, and the [thickness of the antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), which describes a separate
conductor dimension.

items.name: reference_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Reference wavelength of a spectrometer channel is the absolute vacuum
wavelength at the center of its spectral instrument function; a bin-specific
value refers to the center of that detector bin's response.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of spectrometer channel

The reference wavelength is the absolute vacuum wavelength at the center of
the channel's spectral instrument function. It is a response-position
wavelength, distinct from the wavelength of a spectral line or a wavelength
selected as a calibration reference.

The response-center wavelength is defined by

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}} = \operatorname{center}_{\lambda}\!\left[\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\lambda)\right]
$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference wavelength,
$\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{ch}}(\lambda)$ is the channel's spectral instrument
function as a function of $\lambda$, $\lambda$ is [vacuum wavelength], and
$\operatorname{center}_{\lambda}$ denotes the wavelength coordinate at the
center of the response function.

The value applies to the channel response or, when specified for a vertical
detector bin, that bin's response; it is not an average across bins. The
response spread about this center is characterized separately by the [width
of a spectrometer channel](name:width_of_spectrometer_channel). The
[reference calibration wavelength of a spectrometer
channel](name:reference_calibration_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel) is
distinct: it is the zero-pixel intercept of a linear
pixel-to-vacuum-wavelength relation.

items.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
items.description:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
poloidal projection of the electric current contribution associated with
magnetic-field-aligned viscous stress.
items.documentation:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the poloidal direction. Parallel identifies the
viscous-stress mechanism, not the direction of this current component.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_{\mathrm p}^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm p}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the poloidal current-density
contribution, $\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density
vector due to parallel
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and
$\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the oriented local poloidal unit tangent.
The superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity
contribution. The tangent follows a magnetic-flux contour in the
major-radius–vertical plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. Its orientation toward increasing poloidal angle must be
specified by the poloidal-angle convention.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
poloidal current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution, whose poloidal projection is [poloidal
current density due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity).

Poloidal and magnetic-field-aligned directions are distinct: [parallel
current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) projects
the same parent vector onto the local magnetic-field direction instead.

Sign convention: Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution has a component along the poloidal tangent toward increasing
poloidal angle.

items.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description:
X-axis component of a camera's unit viewing-direction vector in the
right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed projection of a camera’s line-of-sight direction
unit vector onto the Cartesian x axis. It specifies one component of the
camera viewing orientation.

If $\hat{\mathbf d}_{\rm cam}$ is the camera’s line-of-sight direction unit
vector and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the x-axis unit vector, the component is
defined by:

$$
d_x = \hat{\mathbf d}_{\rm cam} \cdot \hat{\mathbf x}
$$

Here $d_x$ is this quantity, $\hat{\mathbf d}_{\rm cam}$ is the camera
direction vector, and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the unit vector along increasing
x in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ frame. The
corresponding y- and z-axis components are given by [y-direction unit vector
of camera](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-direction unit
vector of camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera); these components
together specify the viewing direction and satisfy unit-vector
normalization.

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian (x̂, ŷ, ẑ) basis of the unit
direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the neutron detector
center, with ẑ vertical. It is the vertical direction cosine, not a
position coordinate.
items.documentation:
Z component in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$
basis of the unit direction vector from each field-of-view voxel to the
neutron detector center is the projection of that voxel-to-detector
direction onto the vertical basis vector $\hat{z}$. It represents the
vertical direction cosine of the ray from the voxel toward the detector
center.

The component is defined by the normalized displacement from the voxel
position to the detector-center position:

$$
u_z = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v) \cdot \hat{z}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_d - \mathbf{r}_v \rVert}
$$

where $u_z$ is the z component of the direction unit vector, $\mathbf{r}_v$
is the field-of-view voxel position, $\mathbf{r}_d$ is the neutron
detector-center position, and $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis.

Together with
[x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector)
and
[y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector),
it forms the direction-cosine triplet of the same voxel-to-detector ray, so
$u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ and $-1 \le u_z \le 1$. This quantity is a
direction cosine, not a vertical position coordinate or displacement
magnitude; it is the neutron-detector analog of
[z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera).

items.name: ion_momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Diamagnetic-drift contribution to the local ion momentum-balance source,
summed over ion charge states and resolved for the represented momentum
projection.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to an area-normalized
local source in the ion linear-momentum balance. It represents
pressure-gradient-driven transport of the represented momentum projection
and combines the contributions from all ion charge states, excluding neutral
momentum.

$$
S_{i,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \sum_Z S_{i,Z,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $S_{i,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the aggregate ion momentum source,
$S_{i,Z,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is its contribution for ionic charge state
$Z$, and $\ell$ denotes the represented linear-momentum projection. This is
the ion-specific contribution to the generic [momentum source due to
diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), distinct
from the associated [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

Sign convention: Positive when diamagnetic-drift momentum transfer acts in
the positive direction of the represented momentum projection.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_launching_position
items.description:
Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the
physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched, measured
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame with R major radius, φ
toroidal angle, and Z vertical height.
items.documentation:
Toroidal angle of launching position is the azimuthal coordinate of the
physical point where a heating wave or particle beam is launched. It is
defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a launch point whose horizontal Cartesian coordinates are expressed in a
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $+\hat{x}$ defining $\phi=0$, the toroidal angle is

$$
\phi_\mathrm{launch} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_\mathrm{launch}, x_\mathrm{launch}) \bmod 2\pi
$$

where $x_\mathrm{launch}$ and $y_\mathrm{launch}$ are the horizontal
Cartesian coordinates of the launch point, in meters, and
$\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the quadrant-resolved azimuth.

This quantity specifies only the toroidal location of the launch point. The
vertical coordinate of the same point is
[vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position),
while steering or propagation orientation is represented by direction
quantities such as
[toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam](name:toroidal_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_beam);
this quantity is not a beam direction or wave-vector angle. Values differing
by integer multiples of $2\pi$ identify the same toroidal locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the angular displacement from the $\phi=0$
direction is counter-clockwise as viewed from the $+\hat{Z}$ side looking
toward decreasing $Z$.

items.name: atomic_mass
items.description:
Atomic mass is the mass assigned per neutral reference atom of a specified
elemental or isotopic composition, including its bound electrons.
items.documentation:
Atomic mass is the mass assigned to one neutral reference atom of a
specified element or isotope. It characterizes isotopic composition and
includes the bound-electron contribution of the neutral atom.

The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by

$$
m = A_{\mathrm r}\,m_{\mathrm u}
$$

where $m$ is the atomic mass, $A_{\mathrm r}$ is the corresponding relative
atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant, defined as one
twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground
state.

The value applies per constituent atom, not to the complete mass of a
molecule or the total mass of a particle population. For a specified
isotopic mixture, it denotes the atom-number-weighted mean of the
constituent isotope masses. It is independent of ionic charge state and
differs from the charge-dependent rest mass of an ion. It is a physical
mass, not the integer nucleon count called the mass number, a mass density,
or a mass flow rate.

The [neutral-beam atomic mass](name:neutral_beam_atomic_mass) specializes
this definition to atoms of the beam species. In contrast, [atomic
number](name:atomic_number) identifies the nuclear proton count and does not
distinguish isotopes of the same element.

items.name: power_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
items.description:
Power carried by neutral-beam particles that traverse the plasma without
ionization or stopping and exit through the far plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
The neutral-beam shine-through power is the energy carried per unit time by
injected neutral particles that cross the plasma without ionization or
another stopping interaction and leave through the far plasma boundary. It
includes only the outgoing neutral energy that is not deposited in the
plasma.

The defining outward energy-flux integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{st}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{far}}} \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{st}}$ is the shine-through power,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{E,n}$ is the energy-flux vector carried by the exiting
neutral particles, $A_{\mathrm{far}}$ is the far plasma-boundary surface,
and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is its outward unit normal. It is excluded from the
power absorbed by the plasma from a neutral beam injector.

items.name: neutral_source_rate
items.description:
Neutral source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net gain or loss of
particles of a specified neutral species per physical volume and time.
items.documentation:
Neutral source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which
particles enter or leave a specified neutral species. It supplies the
particle-number source term in that species' density continuity equation.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_0(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_0$ is the neutral source rate, $S_{0,\mathrm{gain}}$ and
$S_{0,\mathrm{loss}}$ are the nonnegative local rates of neutral particle
production and removal, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity is summed over all internal states of the specified neutral
atomic or molecular species, not over different species. It combines
contributing source and sink processes, including ionization losses and
recombination gains. Charge exchange contributes through its net effect on
the specified species; transitions solely between its neutral internal
states cancel in the state sum. Charged particles are excluded, and the rate
is not integrated over the enclosed plasma volume.

The divergence of the [neutral particle flux](name:neutral_particle_flux)
supplies the spatial-transport term in the same continuity equation, whereas
this source describes particle production or removal. Unlike the [thermal
particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), this quantity
selects its population by charge neutrality rather than membership in a
thermal population.

Sign convention: Positive when contributing processes produce a net gain of
particles of the specified neutral species; negative values indicate net
removal.

items.name: toroidal_neon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of neon ions, averaged over ionic
charge states and evaluated at the radial location of the internal transport
barrier.
items.documentation:
The neon-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted mean flow of all neon
ion charge states at the radial location assigned to the internal transport
barrier; neutral neon is excluded.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included neon ionic charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is its flow-velocity component along the
geometric toroidal unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity is the toroidal counterpart of the
radial-location-specific
[toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis](name:toroidal_neon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and uses the same charge-state aggregation convention as the analogous
[toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the neon-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_neutral_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed radial component of the effective convection velocity multiplying
neutral-particle density in the advective part of edge-plasma transport.
items.documentation:
Radial neutral-particle convection velocity is the effective coefficient of
the density-proportional advective flux of neutral particles in edge-plasma
transport. It represents directed drift, pinch, or outward convection after
density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated.

The radial convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,r}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_n v_{n,r}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial particle flux due to
convection, $n_n$ is the neutral-particle number density, and $v_{n,r}$ is
this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to the neutral-particle channel in the edge plasma and
is the radial component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. It is an effective coefficient for the named
neutral-particle population, not a sum of energy or momentum transport
coefficients.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and is
distinct from the full
[neutral_particle_convection_velocity](name:neutral_particle_convection_velocity),
which has no directional projection. The
[parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity)
represents the corresponding projection along the magnetic field rather than
along increasing major radius.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-particle convective velocity
points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the
magnetic axis, taken as the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge
states Li+, Li2+, and Li3+. Neutral lithium is excluded.
items.documentation:
Density-weighted toroidal fluid velocity of lithium impurity ions at the
magnetic axis is the local toroidal component of the lithium impurity-ion
fluid velocity at the magnetic axis. The magnetic axis is the innermost
flux-surface locus where the poloidal magnetic flux has an extremum. Because
this is an intensive species-level quantity, the charge-state aggregation is
the density-weighted mean over lithium ion charge states $\mathrm{Li}^{+}$,
$\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$, and $\mathrm{Li}^{3+}$; neutral lithium is excluded.

The density-weighted toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Li}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the lithium ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is
the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is
its fluid velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major radius and $Z$ the vertical height.

This is a local on-axis value, not a flux-surface average or a boundary
value. The analogous local lithium-ion quantities include
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and
[toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top](name:toroidal_lithium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted lithium-ion flow points
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser
items.description:
Toroidal angle locating the endpoint of a Thomson-scattering laser in the
right-handed cylindrical frame (R, φ, Z).
items.documentation:
The toroidal coordinate φ identifies the azimuthal location of the
Thomson-scattering laser endpoint about the machine symmetry axis. Together
with the corresponding radial coordinate, it locates the endpoint in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.

The endpoint position is represented as

$$
\mathbf r_{\rm end}=R_{\rm end}\,\hat{\mathbf R}(\phi_{\rm end})+Z_{\rm end}\,\hat{\mathbf Z}
$$

where $\mathbf r_{\rm end}$ is the endpoint position, $R_{\rm end}$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $\phi_{\rm end}$ is this toroidal coordinate,
$Z_{\rm end}$ is its vertical coordinate, and $\hat{\mathbf R}$ and
$\hat{\mathbf Z}$ are the cylindrical radial and vertical unit vectors. The
radial counterpart is the [radial coordinate of the Thomson-scattering
laser](name:radial_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser).

Sign convention: Positive when the angular displacement is counter-clockwise
viewed from above along the positive $Z$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: carbon_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for carbon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of the carbon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the carbon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local carbon-ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the carbon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{C}^{+}}$ is the number of carbon ions in all positive ionization
states, and $V$ is a small plasma volume whose center approaches the sheath
entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to carbon ions immediately upstream of the
electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all positive
carbon ionization states, from singly ionized through fully stripped carbon.
Neutral carbon atoms, carbon-bearing neutral molecules, electrons, and ions
of other elements are excluded.

Unlike [carbon_density](name:carbon_density), which has the broader
elemental-carbon scope including neutral carbon, this quantity is restricted
to the charge-state-summed positive-ion population at the divertor target.

items.name: vector_potential
items.description:
Magnetic vector-potential quantity covering the full potential, its
directional components, and fluctuations about an equilibrium potential.
items.documentation:
The magnetic vector potential is a vector field whose spatial curl
determines the associated magnetic field. A perturbation denotes the
departure from an equilibrium vector potential and may be represented by a
reference-scaled amplitude.

$$
\mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector-potential field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
its associated magnetic-field vector, and $\nabla \times$ is the spatial
curl operator. The potential is gage-dependent: replacing $\mathbf{A}$ by
$\mathbf{A} + \nabla\chi$, where $\chi$ is a scalar gage function, leaves
$\mathbf{B}$ unchanged. The family includes directional components such as
the [radial vector potential](name:radial_vector_potential) and [poloidal
vector potential](name:poloidal_vector_potential), as well as the perturbed
vector potential.

Sign convention: Positive when a specified gage-fixed component points along
its corresponding positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ increases away from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
increases toroidally, and $Z$ increases vertically.

items.name: resistance_of_shunt
items.description:
Lumped ohmic resistance of the selected shunt resistor, relating its
terminal voltage to the current flowing through that shunt.
items.documentation:
The shunt resistance is the lumped electrical opposition between the
terminals of the selected shunt resistor. It characterizes one shunt member
used to relate its terminal voltage to the current flowing through it.

For nonzero shunt current, the resistance is defined by

$$
R_{\mathrm{sh}} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{sh}}}{I_{\mathrm{sh}}}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the selected shunt resistance, $V_{\mathrm{sh}}$
is the terminal voltage represented by [voltage of
shunt](name:voltage_of_shunt), and $I_{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the current through
the selected shunt.

The quantity applies to the individual selected shunt and is a lumped
circuit property; it is not a material resistivity, the resistance of the
entire divertor or vessel structure, or the shunt terminal voltage itself.
The associated current can be inferred from the terminal voltage as
$I_{\mathrm{sh}} = V_{\mathrm{sh}} / R_{\mathrm{sh}}$, so the resistance and
[voltage of shunt](name:voltage_of_shunt) jointly define this
current-inference relationship.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the magnetic axis specifies its signed height above
or below the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the magnetic axis is its signed height relative to
the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis height,
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the position vector of a point on the
magnetic axis relative to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is
the unit vector along the positive vertical direction, parallel to the
toroidal symmetry axis.

This quantity is a coordinate of the magnetic axis, not a height averaged
