over the plasma or the [vertical coordinate of an
X-point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_x_point), which refers to a different
equilibrium location.

In an axisymmetric equilibrium, this coordinate and the major-radius
coordinate of the magnetic axis together specify its position in a poloidal
cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic axis lies on the $+Z$ side of
the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux
surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},
Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic
field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the
nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
items.description:
Vector conventional electric-current density attributed to turbulence-driven
anomalous transport in a plasma.
items.documentation:
Current density due to anomalous transport is the vector conventional
electric-current density associated with turbulent, nonclassical transport
processes that produce a net charge flow. It denotes only the
anomalous-transport contribution to the plasma current, not the total
current density.

This is a phenomenological transport-current contribution; no universal
closed-form constitutive identity is part of its definition. The vector may
be resolved into
[radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:radial_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport),
[toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport),
and
[vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, and into
[parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
along the local magnetic-field direction $\hat{b} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field. It is
distinct from
[current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity),
which represents a perpendicular-viscous transport-current contribution.

items.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
items.description:
Normalized gyrotropic pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle
distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components
parallel and perpendicular to the background magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The normalized particle perturbed pressure is a gyrotropic vector quantity
representing the pressure fluctuation of the physical particle population in
a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, decomposed into components parallel and
perpendicular to the equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, each expressed
dimensionlessly as a ratio to a reference thermal pressure $p_\mathrm{ref}$.

For species $s$, the parallel and perpendicular components are the second
velocity-space moments of the perturbed particle distribution function
$\delta f_s$:

$$
\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} = \frac{m_s}{p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\parallel^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v, \qquad \hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2 \, p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2 \, \delta f_s \, d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are velocities
parallel and perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$, and $p_\mathrm{ref} =
n_\mathrm{ref} T_\mathrm{ref}$ is evaluated at the outboard midplane.

Unlike the corresponding gyroaveraged gyrocenter perturbed pressure, this
quantity is built from the full particle distribution function, implicitly
incorporating finite-Larmor-radius corrections through the
particle-to-gyrocenter coordinate transformation. The isotropic scalar
parent particle_perturbed_pressure is recovered as the trace average
$\hat{p}_s = (\hat{p}_{\parallel,s} + 2\hat{p}_{\perp,s})/3$. The
parallel_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure and
[perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure)
components together encode the pressure anisotropy of the eigenmode, with
the ratio $\hat{p}_{\parallel,s}/\hat{p}_{\perp,s}$ quantifying deviation
from local thermodynamic equilibrium relevant to mirror-mode and fire-hose
stability.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume
from co-passing nonthermal particles to thermal ions of one specified
species and charge state.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the signed
rate of kinetic-energy transfer from co-passing nonthermal particles to
thermal ions of one specified species and charge state, averaged over a
magnetic flux surface. The co-passing restriction selects untrapped donor
orbits; it does not restrict the receiving thermal ions to that orbit class.

The defining relation is the flux-surface average of the receiving
population's collisional kinetic-energy moment:

$$
P_{iq,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \int \frac{1}{2}m_i |\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,d}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_d^{\mathrm{co}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

Here $P_{iq,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the co-passing thermal-ion
charge-state collisional power density, $i$ identifies the receiving ion
species, $q$ identifies its ionic charge number, and $d$ identifies the
designated nonthermal donor population. The symbol $m_i$ is the
receiving-ion mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is
receiving-ion velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration
measure. The distributions $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $f_d^{\mathrm{co}}$
describe the receiving thermal ions and the co-passing donor component,
respectively. The operator $C_{iq,d}$ gives the collisional time derivative
of the receiving distribution caused by Coulomb collisions with that donor
component, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes
magnetic-flux-surface averaging.

This quantity includes one receiving species and charge state, with no
charge-state sum. It excludes energy transferred to thermal electrons or
fast-ion recipients and represents an energy-exchange rate, not stored
kinetic energy or volume-integrated power. Summing over all ionic charge
states of the receiving species yields [co-passing thermal-ion collisional
power density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions)
at the same averaging level.

Adding this contribution to the
[counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and
[trapped](name:trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
contributions yields the flux-surface average of [thermal-ion charge-state
collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions),
which includes all donor orbit classes.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy
into the receiving thermal ions of the specified species and charge state.

items.name: neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming
upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density component-by-component
in edge-plasma transport closures.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum coefficient is the neutral-particle specialization of
the general momentum_coefficient vector, providing one dimensionless limiter
factor per spatial direction for neutral momentum transport in multi-fluid
edge plasma models. Each directional component independently bounds the
corresponding neutral momentum flux density, preventing unphysical
exceedance of the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is
large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The component $\alpha_\alpha$ in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ is defined as
the ratio of the modeled flux to its free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_\alpha = \frac{\Pi_\alpha}{\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free}}
$$

where $\Pi_\alpha$ is the modeled neutral momentum flux density in direction
$\hat{e}_\alpha$ and $\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free} = m_n n_n u_\alpha^{\rm free}$
is the free-streaming estimate, with $m_n$ the neutral particle mass, $n_n$
the neutral number density, and $u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ the direction-$\alpha$
free-streaming reference speed. The constraint $\alpha_\alpha \in [0, 1]$
ensures the closure preserves the sign of the momentum flux while bounding
its magnitude. The field-aligned component is analogous to
parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient, which resolves the same
quantity by internal neutral state.

Components are computed within edge-plasma transport closures as a function
of local collisionality; values near 1 characterize the collision-dominated
limit, while values near 0 indicate strongly free-streaming conditions where
the limiter actively constrains the flux.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density
of a specified neutral internal state, directed along increasing poloidal
angle θ in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ).
items.documentation:
Poloidal effective velocity for convective transport of the energy density
of a specified neutral internal state is the component of the effective
convection velocity along the tangent direction of increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. It is the
poloidal directional realization of the [neutral internal-state energy
convection
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity).

For the poloidal transport direction, the convective energy-flux component
is defined by

$$
q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} = u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}} w_{E,\nu}
$$

where $q_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the poloidal convective
energy-flux component, $u_{E,\nu,\theta}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this poloidal
effective convection velocity, $w_{E,\nu}$ is the energy density of the
neutral internal state, and $\nu$ identifies that state.

The quantity applies to the specified state and does not sum over all
neutral internal states. It is the poloidal member of the directional set
that also includes the radial neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity and the [field-aligned neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity);
by contrast, neutral species energy convection velocity represents the
corresponding energy transport aggregated over a neutral species.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective velocity points in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate
system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, making the convective energy flux positive in
that direction.

items.name: ratio_of_total_ion_density_to_electron_density
items.description:
Ratio of total ion number density to free-electron number density, summing
ions over all species and positive charge states and including thermal and
nonthermal populations in both densities.
items.documentation:
Ratio of total ion number density to free-electron number density at the
same plasma location and time. It expresses the abundance of all ion
particles relative to free electrons, rather than their relative electric
charge or mass.

The local ratio is defined as

$$
R_{i/e} = \frac{n_{i,\mathrm{total}}}{n_e} = \frac{\sum_s\sum_{z\geq 1} n_{s,z}}{n_e}
$$

where $R_{i/e}$ denotes this abundance ratio, $n_{i,\mathrm{total}}$ is the
total ion number density, $n_e$ is the [free-electron number
density](name:electron_density), $s$ indexes ion species, $z$ is the
positive ionic charge number, and $n_{s,z}$ is the [ion charge-state number
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) for species $s$ and charge state
$z$. Each sum includes all populated positive charge states of the
corresponding species.

Both densities include thermal and nonthermal populations. The numerator is
summed over all ion species and charge states without charge weighting;
neutral particles are excluded. The denominator counts free electrons and
excludes bound electrons. This is a local ratio, not a ratio of spatially
averaged densities or a spatial average of local ratios, and it is defined
only when $n_e>0$.

Unlike the [species-specific ion-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_ion_density_to_electron_density), this quantity
includes every ion species. It is not an effective-charge measure or the
ratio of positive charge density to electron charge-density magnitude.

For a plasma whose charge carriers are positive ions and free electrons,
quasineutrality gives $n_e\simeq\sum_s\sum_{z\geq1}z\,n_{s,z}$.
Consequently, this ratio is approximately the reciprocal of the
ion-number-density-weighted [average charge
number](name:average_charge_number) over the complete ion population.
Multiply charged ions can therefore make it less than unity without implying
a departure from quasineutrality.

items.name: volume_averaged_argon_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged number density of argon ions over the confined plasma
volume, summed over all ionization stages.
items.documentation:
The volume-averaged argon ion number density is the spatial mean of the
local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) throughout the confined plasma
volume, including contributions from every argon ionization stage. It is
distinct from a local or charge-state-resolved density.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Ar}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\mathrm{p}}\int_{V_\mathrm{p}} n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element, and $n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r})$
is the local argon ion density. The local density is charge-state summed,
$n_\mathrm{Ar}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r})$,
where $q$ is the argon ionization stage. This quantity provides the
argon-density numerator for the impurity concentration ratio [ratio of
volume-averaged argon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_argon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

items.name: magnetic_shear_at_flux_surface
items.description:
Magnetic shear at a flux surface is the logarithmic derivative of the safety
factor with respect to the outward normalized toroidal flux radius.
items.documentation:
Magnetic shear at flux surface

The defining relation is

$$
\hat{s} = \frac{\rho}{q}\frac{dq}{d\rho}
$$

where $\hat{s}$ is the magnetic shear at the specified flux surface, $q$ is
the safety factor, and $\rho$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius
increasing outward from the magnetic axis. The derivative is taken with
respect to that coordinate.

This quantity is a single flux-surface evaluation, not an average over
neighboring flux surfaces or an integral across a plasma region. The
definition requires a nonzero safety factor and an existing derivative. It
is distinct from the unnormalized safety-factor derivative and from magnetic
shear defined using geometric minor radius; a nonlinear change of radial
label generally changes the shear.

The [magnetic shear at an internal transport
barrier](name:magnetic_shear_at_internal_transport_barrier) is a
locus-specific specialization of this quantity, using the same defining
relation at the barrier's flux-surface location.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a
nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$,
$\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Toroidal bulk-flow velocity of hydrogen ions evaluated at the radial
location identified with the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk flow projected onto the toroidal
direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier. It
describes directed ion motion and excludes neutral-hydrogen motion.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity and
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity is evaluated on the
flux-surface radius assigned to the internal transport barrier and is the
hydrogen counterpart of
[toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the shatter-cone origin, locating its reference
point by perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a shatter-cone origin is the major-radius location
of that geometric reference point relative to the toroidal symmetry axis. It
is the $R$ coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
with basis vectors $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ satisfying $\hat{R}
\times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies specifically to the origin of the elliptic shatter
cone. It denotes one geometric coordinate of that reference point, with no
averaging, integration, or aggregation over the cone surface, its axis, or
injected fragments; it is distinct from radial coordinates assigned to other
injector features or positions.

It is a locus-specific specialization of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): the parent defines the major-radius
coordinate generally, while this quantity evaluates it at the shatter-cone
origin.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the deuterium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local deuterium-ion count per physical volume there,
summed over all deuterium ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the deuterium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local deuterium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all deuterium ionic charge states. It represents
deuterium ions specifically, rather than neutral deuterium, electrons, or
another ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{D,\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_D}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{D,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the deuterium ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_D$ is the number of deuterium ions summed over all ionic
charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete deuterium ion population at that
location and is charge-state-summed; it is neither a flux-surface or volume
integral nor a neutral, electron, or other-ion density.

This is the deuterium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It must be
distinguished from [hydrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts hydrogen ions
rather than deuterium ions.

items.name: vertical_ion_velocity
items.description:
Directed flow of a specified ion species along the toroidal symmetry axis,
defined as the number-density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion velocity is the local projection of the bulk [ion
velocity](name:ion_velocity) onto the symmetry-axis direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projection and charge-state average are defined by

$$
u_{i,Z}=\mathbf{u}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}=\frac{\sum_q n_{i,q}\,\mathbf{u}_{i,q}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{\sum_q n_{i,q}}
$$

where $u_{i,Z}$ is the vertical ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_i$ is the
charge-state-averaged ion bulk velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit
vector along the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. The index $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $q$ indexes its ionic charge states,
$n_{i,q}$ is the number density of each state, and $\mathbf{u}_{i,q}$ is
that state's bulk velocity.

For the edge-plasma ion population, this is a local directed-flow component,
not a spatial average, velocity magnitude, or thermal velocity spread. It
excludes neutral particles and other ion species. The [vertical ion
charge-state velocity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity) retains
individual charge-state resolution; this quantity combines those components
through a density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not a sum of
velocities.

Unlike [vertical plasma velocity](name:vertical_plasma_velocity), which
projects the mass-weighted center-of-mass flow of all contributing plasma
species, this component describes only the selected ion species.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion bulk flow has a component toward
increasing $Z$.

items.name: normal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Signed coordinate of each toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section
outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret normal, perpendicular to the
conductor centerline and binormal directions.
items.documentation:
The normal coordinate is the signed location of a toroidal-field-coil
conductor cross-section outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret normal.
The cross-section lies in the plane perpendicular to the conductor
centerline, so this coordinate resolves displacement along one local
transverse direction.

For a vertex at centerline position $s$, the defining relation is:

$$
x_n(s) = \left[\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_c(s)\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}(s)
$$

where $x_n$ is the normal coordinate in m, $s$ is centerline arc length in
m, $\mathbf{r}_v$ and $\mathbf{r}_c(s)$ are the vertex and centerline
position vectors in m, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}(s)$ is the local Frenet–Serret
normal unit vector.

Together with the [binormal coordinate of the toroidal field
coil](name:binormal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil), this coordinate
specifies the conductor outline in the local cross-sectional plane. It is
distinct from a radial coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame and has the same geometric role as the [normal coordinate of the
correction coil](name:normal_coordinate_of_correction_coil).

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement has a positive
projection onto the local Frenet–Serret normal unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}(s)$.

items.name: line_averaged_iron_density
items.description:
Line-averaged iron density is the path-length mean of total iron
impurity-ion number density, summed over Fe1+ through Fe26+.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged iron density is the chord-length mean of the total iron ion
number density along a specified line of sight. It includes all ionization
states from Fe$^{1+}$ through Fe$^{26+}$ and does not resolve their
individual contributions.

The line average is defined as

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,line}}$ is the line-averaged density,
$n_{\mathrm{Fe}}(l)$ is the local iron ion number density at path coordinate
$l$, and $L$ is the total chord length.

The local quantity being averaged is the charge-state-summed [iron
density](name:iron_density). This chord average is distinct from
[line_averaged_argon_density](name:line_averaged_argon_density), which
applies the same path averaging to argon ions, and from a volume-averaged
iron density, which averages over a plasma volume rather than a line of
sight.

items.name: carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron carbon source rate delivered to the plasma
vessel by gas injection systems, with each injected carbon atom contributing
six equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The carbon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous
rate at which neutral carbon with atomic number six is admitted to the
plasma vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. It is the carbon-specific component of [source rate due to gas
injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

For carbon injection, the defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}} = 6\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the raw carbon-atom delivery rate; both rates have
units of inverse seconds.

This quantity counts injected carbon atoms, not electrons currently present
in the plasma, carbon ionization states, or the net carbon balance after
transport and removal. Its time integral gives [accumulated carbon count due
to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
same equivalent-electron convention applies to [tritium source rate due to
gas injection](name:tritium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), with a
different atomic-number factor.

Sign convention: Positive when carbon gas is delivered into the vessel,
increasing the equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: carbon_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Carbon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of carbon ions, summed over all ionization states and
excluding neutral carbon.
items.documentation:
Carbon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of carbon ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed carbon-ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{C}} = \sum_{z=1}^{6} n_{\mathrm{C}}^{z+}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the total carbon-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{C}}^{z+}$ is the number density of carbon ions with charge state
$z+$, and $z$ is the integer carbon-ion charge state.

This quantity applies locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined
by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all carbon ionization states from C$^{+}$ through C$^{6+}$,
excludes neutral carbon, and is not line-, volume-, or
flux-surface-averaged.

It is the carbon-species component of the total [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [carbon density at the
limiter](name:carbon_density_at_limiter), it is evaluated at the
pedestal-top locus rather than adjacent to a limiter surface.

items.name: parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized
diffusive thermal-energy flux of the ion population to the local
ion-temperature gradient along magnetic field lines.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion energy diffusion coefficient quantifies gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the ion population,
providing the Fick's-law proportionality between the density-normalized
diffusive parallel ion heat flux and the ion-temperature gradient along
magnetic field lines. It is the field-aligned component of the
direction-agnostic [ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient), excluding convective
and other non-Fickian heat-flux contributions.

The defining Fickian relation for the parallel diffusive ion thermal-energy
flux is:

$$
Q_{i,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}} = -n_i D_{i,E,\parallel} \nabla_\parallel T_i
$$

where $Q_{i,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive ion
thermal-energy flux, $n_i$ is the ion number density associated with the
modeled ion population, $D_{i,E,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion energy
diffusion coefficient, $T_i$ is the corresponding ion temperature, and
$\nabla_\parallel T_i$ is its derivative along the magnetic-field direction.
The coefficient does not select a particular charge state or impose the
total-ion aggregation represented by [parallel total ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient);
[parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is
the charge-state-resolved counterpart.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged rate of toroidal angular-momentum transfer per plasma
volume to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions with a
specified ion species.
items.documentation:
Toroidal counter-passing fast-ion collisional torque density is the
flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum transfer rate per plasma
volume delivered to counter-passing fast ions through Coulomb collisions
with a specified ion species.

It is related to the full [counter-passing fast-ion torque density due to
collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by

$$
\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}\cdot\hat{\phi} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the averaged toroidal torque
density, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{cp,coll}}$ is the local collisional
torque-density vector acting on counter-passing fast ions, and the angle
brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic
flux surface. The subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{cp}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$
identify ions, the counter-passing restriction, and collisions,
respectively. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

The orbit restriction applies to the fast-ion distribution, not to the
collision partners. Co-passing and trapped fast-ion contributions are
excluded; co-passing contributions belong instead to [co-passing fast-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
Charge-state contributions are summed at the species level, rather than
resolved for one ionic charge state, while different collision-partner
species remain separate.

This is a toroidal component of [torque density](name:torque_density), not
the full vector or a volume-integrated torque. The local toroidal projection
is taken before flux-surface averaging.

Sign convention: Positive when the collisional torque acting on the fast
ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: line_averaged_hydrogen_density
items.description:
Line-averaged number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma,
giving the path-length-normalized H+ concentration along a specified chord.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged hydrogen density quantifies the mean concentration of
protium ions along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the
path-integrated hydrogen ion content normalized by the chord length.

The line average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_H = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl
$$

where $\overline{n}_H$ is the line-averaged hydrogen density,
$n_H(\mathbf{r}(l))$ is the local protium-ion number density at position
$\mathbf{r}(l)$ along the chord, $l$ is the path-length coordinate,
$\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord, and $L$ is its total length.

The quantity applies to charged protium ions, with any included protium ion
charge states summed before the line average; neutral atomic hydrogen and
heavier hydrogenic isotopes are excluded. It is a chord average rather than
the local [hydrogen density](name:hydrogen_density) at a point or the volume
average represented by
[volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density).

Unlike
[line_averaged_total_ion_density](name:line_averaged_total_ion_density), it
does not include other ion species or hydrogen isotopes. The path-length
normalization preserves the same density meaning as the parent local
quantity while replacing its pointwise value with an average along the
chord.

items.name: vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Gage-dependent vacuum magnetic vector potential generated by external
current sources; its curl gives the magnetic induction when plasma-current
contributions are excluded.
items.documentation:
The vacuum magnetic vector potential is a gage-dependent vector field
representing the external-source contribution to the [magnetic vector
potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential). It excludes the contribution
generated by plasma currents while retaining the gage dependence of the full
potential.

The defining relation between this potential and the corresponding vacuum
magnetic induction is:

$$
\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the vacuum magnetic vector potential,
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the magnetic induction produced by the
external sources alone, and $\nabla \times$ is the curl operator. Replacing
$\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ by $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} + \nabla \chi$,
where $\chi$ is an arbitrary scalar gage function, leaves
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ unchanged.

The vector may be resolved into components in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Its radial and vertical projections are represented by
the [radial vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) and [vertical
vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), respectively.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of the vector points along its
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector
kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of
momentum density carried by neutrals in a specified electronic, vibrational,
or rotational state. Its directional children specify the flux and gradient
direction, not the transported momentum component.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient is the vector
kinematic transport coefficient in Fick's-law down-gradient transport of
momentum density carried by neutrals occupying a specified electronic,
vibrational, or rotational internal state. It is the direction-agnostic
parent whose directional members identify the direction of flux and
gradient, while the transported quantity remains the full momentum vector of
that state-resolved neutral population.

For a diagonal directional member in transport direction $j$, the defining
Fick law is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j} = -D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}\,\frac{\partial \mathbf{M}_{\alpha}}{\partial x_j}
$$

where $\alpha$ denotes the specified neutral internal state,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{\alpha j}$ is the vector diffusive flux
of momentum through surfaces normal to direction $j$,
$D^{\mathrm{mom}}_{\alpha j}$ is the corresponding diagonal momentum
diffusion coefficient, $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$ is the momentum density carried
by neutrals in state $\alpha$, and $x_j$ is a coordinate increasing along
the flux and gradient direction. The superscript $\mathrm{mom}$ labels
momentum transport, not a transported momentum component; the minus sign
gives down-gradient transport of each component of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$.

This parent covers diagonal directional coefficients only: a directional
qualifier selects $j$, the flux and gradient direction, and not a component
of $\mathbf{M}_{\alpha}$; off-diagonal tensor transport, where a gradient
along one direction contributes to flux through another, is outside this
standard name. The radial and toroidal directional children use $\hat{R}$
and $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height;
the poloidal directional child uses the direction tangent to the poloidal
circuit in a meridional plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$.

The defining gradient is the gradient of internal-state momentum density; a
form proportional only to a neutral velocity gradient represents the same
coefficient only when the state-resolved mass density is uniform or treated
outside the gradient. This quantity belongs to the [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) family, has the same internal-state
resolution as internal-state momentum diffusion coefficient, differs from
[neutral momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) by resolving the
neutral population by internal state, and differs from [neutral
internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) by
transporting momentum rather than energy.

items.name: boron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary, evaluated as the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume on the last closed magnetic
flux surface, summed over neutral atoms and all ionization states.
items.documentation:
Number density of boron at the plasma boundary is the local, intensive
particle count per physical volume for elemental boron evaluated on the last
closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the limiting closed
magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line
scrape-off-layer region.

The local elemental-boron number density at a boundary point is the zeroth
velocity moment summed over neutral boron and all ionic charge states:

$$
n_{\mathrm B}(\mathbf{x}_b,t) = \sum_{z=0}^{5} \int f_{\mathrm B,z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm B}$ is the elemental-boron number density, $\mathrm B$
denotes boron, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the last closed magnetic flux
surface, $t$ is time, $z$ is the boron charge-state index with $z=0$
denoting neutral boron and $z=1$ through $5$ denoting the ionic states,
$f_{\mathrm B,z}$ is the phase-space distribution function for that state,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element.

This quantity applies specifically to elemental boron and includes neutral
atoms together with all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+. It
is a local value at the plasma boundary, with no averaging over the boundary
surface or over a volume, and excludes densities of other elements and
electrons. Unlike ion_density_at_plasma_boundary, it is not restricted to
charged ions.

It is the boron-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The related
[flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_boron_density_at_plasma_boundary)
applies the same neutral-plus-ionic boron aggregation but averages the
density over the last closed magnetic flux surface rather than giving the
local boundary value.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_active_wall_point
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the active wall point where the plasma boundary
contacts the wall, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the major-radius location of the active wall point, defined
as the point where the plasma boundary is in contact with the wall. It
identifies one specific plasma–wall contact location rather than a general
wall or boundary position.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the coordinate is
defined from the horizontal Cartesian position of the contact point by

$$
R_{\mathrm{active}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{active}}^2+y_{\mathrm{active}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{active}}$ is the major-radius coordinate, and
$x_{\mathrm{active}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{active}}$ are the horizontal Cartesian
coordinates of the active wall point in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This is a pointwise coordinate for the active wall contact and is neither an
average nor a coordinate sequence describing a contour. It is a
locus-specific specialization of
[radial_coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), retaining the same major-radius
meaning while fixing the active wall point as its locus. It differs from
[radial_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point](name:radial_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point),
which refers specifically to the wall point nearest the plasma boundary, and
from
[radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary](name:radial_outline_of_plasma_boundary),
which describes coordinates along the boundary outline.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque-density vector transferred to counter-passing fast ions
in a specified charge state by Coulomb collisions with background plasma
particles.
items.documentation:
The collisional torque-density vector for counter-passing fast ions in
charge state $q$ quantifies the angular-momentum source per unit volume
arising from Coulomb collisions with background plasma particles.

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{q}^{\mathrm{cp}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{q,\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the
torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{q}^{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the
angular-momentum density of the counter-passing fast-ion population in
charge state $q$, and the subscript indicates the collisional contribution.

The quantity includes only transfer to the specified counter-passing
fast-ion charge-state population; it excludes co-passing and thermal-ion
populations and noncollisional transfer. It is the counter-passing component
of the broader
[fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
while
[co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
represents the corresponding co-passing branch.

The vector components are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive components point along the corresponding positive
$R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
basis.

items.name: reference_phase
items.description:
Reference phase is the signed angular offset that fixes the phase origin of
a complex oscillatory perturbation relative to a chosen zero-phase
reference.
items.documentation:
Reference phase is the signed angular offset that sets the phase origin for
a complex oscillatory perturbation relative to a chosen zero-phase
reference. It parameterizes a phase gage: changing it rotates the complex
amplitude without changing invariant perturbation properties such as
magnitude, growth rate, or eigenfunction shape.

A perturbation quantity $\tilde{q}$ whose zero-phase representation is
$\tilde{q}_0$ is shifted by the reference phase $\alpha$ as:

$$
\tilde{q} = \tilde{q}_0 \exp(i\alpha)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the reference phase and $\tilde{q}_0$ is the complex
perturbation at the chosen zero-phase reference.

This parent quantity covers reference phases that choose the complex phase
origin of perturbations, including the [mode reference
phase](name:mode_reference_phase). It is not a physical propagation phase, a
geometric position angle, or a phase difference between two independent
signals unless that phase difference specifically defines the chosen
reference offset.

Sign convention: Positive when the applied phase factor advances the
perturbation by increasing its complex argument relative to the zero-phase
reference.

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description:
Real part of the radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the in-phase
coefficient of the R component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame for a complex vacuum magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction of one
toroidal Fourier harmonic.
items.documentation:
Real part of the radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the in-phase
coefficient of the radial component of a complex magnetic-field perturbation
eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma for one
toroidal Fourier harmonic. Radial means projection onto $\hat R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; it is not projection
onto the equilibrium flux-surface-normal direction.

For a complex harmonic amplitude $\delta\tilde{\mathbf
B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x})$, with physical perturbation represented by
$\operatorname{Re}\{\delta\tilde{\mathbf B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x})
e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}\}$, this quantity is defined by:

$$
\delta B^{\mathrm{vac,Re}}_{R,n}(\mathbf{x}) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta\tilde{\mathbf B}^{\mathrm{vac}}_n(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat R\right]
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes real part, $n$ is the toroidal mode
number, $\omega$ is the angular frequency associated with the chosen complex
representation, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\hat R$ is the radial basis
vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The [imaginary
counterpart](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) is
the quadrature coefficient of the same complex radial component, and the two
together specify the [complex radial vacuum perturbation
amplitude](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) for the chosen
eigenfunction phase. This vacuum-region quantity is distinct from the
corresponding plasma-region perturbation; a linear eigenfunction amplitude
is defined only up to an overall complex normalization unless a separate
normalization condition is imposed.

Sign convention: Positive when, at Fourier phase $n\phi-\omega t=0$ for the
representation above, the vacuum magnetic-field perturbation has a component
in the $+\hat R$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame.

items.name: vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile
items.description:
Signed vertical (Z) coordinate of each point on a limiter-tile boundary
contour in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical outline of a limiter tile gives the signed vertical coordinate
of each point on the tile’s geometric boundary contour. It describes the
contour geometry rather than a material property, thickness, or surface-load
quantity.

For contour point $i$, the vertical coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_i = \mathbf{r}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $Z_i$ is the vertical coordinate of point $i$, $\mathbf{r}_i$ is its
position vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies pointwise to the irregular outline of one limiter tile
in its poloidal cross section. The contour is closed by connecting its final
point to its initial point, without duplicating the initial point; no
averaging, summation, or other aggregation over contour points is implied.
Unlike the [radial outline of a limiter
tile](name:radial_outline_of_limiter_tile), this quantity gives the vertical
coordinate rather than the major-radius coordinate of the boundary.

The same geometric carrier and coordinate meaning apply to the [vertical
outline of a divertor tile](name:vertical_outline_of_divertor_tile), but
that related quantity belongs to a divertor tile rather than a limiter tile.

Sign convention: Positive when the contour point lies toward increasing $Z$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization
states.
items.documentation:
Number density of beryllium ions at the plasma boundary is the local,
intensive particle count per physical volume for the beryllium-ion
population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma
boundary is the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining density is the zeroth velocity-space moment, summed over all
beryllium ionization states:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}}\int f_{\mathrm{Be},z}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$
is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ identifies a beryllium
ionization state, $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the set of included
beryllium ionization states, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$f_{\mathrm{Be},z}$ is the velocity distribution function for state $z$, and
$d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies locally at the plasma boundary and is additive over all
included ionic charge states. It includes beryllium ions and excludes
neutral beryllium atoms; it is not a flux-surface average.

This is the beryllium-specific instance of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population is unspecified. It differs from
flux_surface_averaged_beryllium_density_at_plasma_boundary because that
quantity averages the beryllium-ion density over the boundary surface, and
from [beryllium_density_at_limiter](name:beryllium_density_at_limiter),
which uses a limiter-adjacent locus.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description:
Vertical Z-coordinate of the reference point of a lower-hybrid antenna in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate locates the reference point of a lower-hybrid
antenna along the vertical direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation is:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ant}} = Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ant}}$ is the antenna reference point and
$Z(P_{\mathrm{ant}})$ is its vertical coordinate. This quantity refers to
the antenna reference point; the [vertical coordinate of a lower-hybrid
antenna row](name:vertical_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row) refers
instead to a row reference point.

Sign convention: Positive when the antenna reference point lies in the
direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local vector rate of angular-momentum transfer to the thermal-ion population
per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions, restricted to trapped-orbit
contributions and without restricting spatial direction.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal-ion torque density due to collisions is the local torque per
unit volume transferred to the bulk thermal-ion population by Coulomb
collisions with contributing charged-particle populations. It is restricted
to the trapped orbit-class contribution and is not restricted to a single
spatial direction.

For the trapped part of the selected thermal-ion population, the collisional
torque-density vector is defined from its distribution function by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{tr,coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{\mathcal{T}} d^3v\,\bigl(\mathbf{r} \times m_i\mathbf{v}\bigr)\,C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}[f_i](\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is position relative to the torque origin, $m_i$ is the
ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_i$ is the thermal-ion
distribution function, $C_{i,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its Coulomb-collision
operator, and $\mathcal{T}$ is the trapped-orbit region of velocity space.

At parent level, the quantity includes the allowed spatial-direction
components within the trapped orbit class; [toroidal trapped thermal-ion
torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is the corresponding component along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It excludes passing-orbit contributions
and torque deposited in fast-ion populations.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: power_due_to_convection
items.description:
Power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces by convective plasma particle
flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by
streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Convective power quantifies the energy transported to a plasma-facing
surface by the bulk flow of plasma particles — ions, electrons, and neutral
species — streaming along open magnetic field lines from the scrape-off
layer to bounding material surfaces. It represents the convective channel of
the total surface power balance, distinct from the conductive contribution
driven by parallel temperature gradients and from radiative deposition.

The local convective heat-flux density summed over particle species $s$ is

$$
q_{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_s n_s v_{\parallel,s} \left( \frac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_s - 1} k_B T_s + \frac{1}{2} m_s v_{\parallel,s}^2 \right)
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density, $v_{\parallel,s}$ the parallel flow
speed, $\gamma_s$ the adiabatic index (5/3 for monatomic species), $T_s$ the
temperature, and $m_s$ the particle mass. Integrating $q_{\mathrm{conv}}$
over the wetted surface area yields the total convective power in watts.

In experiments the convective power is inferred from Langmuir-probe
measurements of particle flux and sheath-entrance temperature, or decomposed
from total calorimetric measurements by subtracting the conductive fraction
estimated via two-point model analysis. More specific realizations include
[power at a single divertor target due to
convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), [convective
power summed over all divertor
targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection), and [convective power at
the first wall](name:power_at_wall_due_to_convection). The full surface load
integrating all channels is characterized by
heat_flux_of_plasma_facing_component.

items.name: vertical_neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Signed flow along the toroidal symmetry axis, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean vertical velocity of all constituent plasma
species.
items.documentation:
The vertical center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
toroidal symmetry axis. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full
barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},Z} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},Z}$ is the vertical center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the [parent velocity
vector](name:neutral_species_center_of_mass_velocity), $s$ indexes
constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density, and
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$
points along the symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sum includes all species in the local plasma mixture, rather than only
ions or only neutral particles. This is a local mass-density-weighted mean,
not a particle-number-weighted mean or an unweighted sum of species
velocities. The definition requires nonzero total mass density.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its radial and toroidal
components and is distinct from its speed. The vertical direction need not
coincide with the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: incident_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current
items.description:
Incident energy flux at the wall is the incoming energy-transfer rate per
unit area attributable to eddy-current processes, before subtraction of
emitted energy.
items.documentation:
Incident energy flux at the wall due to eddy-current processes is the
incoming contribution to the corresponding surface energy balance. It
describes energy arriving at a wall component before accounting for energy
emitted from that component.

The local incident energy flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}} = \frac{\partial^2 W_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}}{\partial A\,\partial t}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the incident energy flux
attributed to eddy-current processes, $W_{\mathrm{inc}}^{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is
the cumulative incident energy attributed to those processes, $A$ is wall
surface area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to the wall component under consideration and is an
energy-transfer rate per unit area, not a component-integrated power or a
sum over wall components. It includes only the eddy-current-attributed
contribution, not the sum of all incident energy-transfer channels.

Within this mechanism's energy balance, the net flux received by the wall
equals this incident contribution minus the [emitted eddy-current energy
flux]. Incident and emitted contributions are separate nonnegative
directional quantities, unlike their net difference.

items.name: particle_energy
items.description:
Energy-like measure of particle motion in velocity space, combining parallel
and perpendicular kinetic-energy contributions for distribution-based plasma
quantities.
items.documentation:
Particle energy denotes the kinetic-energy content or energy coordinate
associated with a species' velocity-space distribution. It is based on both
parallel and perpendicular motion and can characterize an ordering
coordinate, a distribution moment, or a response of a perturbed
distribution.

The underlying single-particle kinetic energy is

$$
E = \frac{1}{2}m\left(v_\parallel^2 + v_\perp^2\right)
$$

where $E$ is particle kinetic energy, $m$ is particle mass, and
$v_\parallel$ and $v_\perp$ are the velocity components parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field. Distribution-based quantities use
this energy or an equivalent velocity-space weighting;
[fast_particle_energy](name:fast_particle_energy) represents a
fast-population moment, while perturbed_particle_energy represents the
corresponding response of a perturbed distribution. An effective coordinate
may additionally be scaled by a positive reference energy, as in
[effective_particle_energy](name:effective_particle_energy). A moment of a
perturbed distribution may be signed even though the underlying
single-particle kinetic energy is nonnegative.

items.name: edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective kinematic coefficient governing down-gradient transport of a
selected component or projection of aggregate edge-plasma momentum.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective kinematic momentum diffusivity associated
with a selected component or projection of edge-plasma momentum. Edge-plasma
momentum is the aggregate plasma momentum carried in the edge region; the
field-aligned specialization is [parallel edge-plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity).

For a scalar down-gradient closure for selected qualifier $a$, the diffusive
flux of edge-plasma momentum is

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a} = -\rho D_{a} \nabla u_{a}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{a}$ is the diffusive flux vector of
edge-plasma momentum associated with qualifier $a$, $\rho$ is the mass
density of the transported aggregate, $D_{a}$ is this diffusivity, $u_{a}$
is the corresponding edge-plasma velocity component or projection, and
$\nabla$ is the spatial gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient
transport.

The qualifier $a$ identifies the resolved momentum component, projection, or
transport direction; it is not necessarily the direction in which the flux
crosses a surface. The transported aggregate is ion-fluid momentum density
summed over ion species and charge states, excluding electron inertial
momentum, so this quantity is distinct from species-resolved momentum
diffusivities and from non-edge plasma momentum diffusivity.

items.name: lithium_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local number density of lithium ions in the boundary plasma immediately
adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, summed over all positive
ionization states and excluding neutral lithium atoms.
items.documentation:
Lithium density at a limiter is the local number density of lithium ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density in m$^{-3}$,
$N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the counted number of lithium ions, $V$ is volume in
m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the evaluation position in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The quantity is summed over all positive lithium ionization states and
excludes neutral lithium atoms. It is the lithium-specific specialization of
[density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from the broader
ion density at a limiter, which does not select lithium.

items.name: pedestal_thermal_electron_energy
items.description:
Volume-integrated random kinetic energy of bulk thermal electrons within the
plasma pedestal, excluding suprathermal electrons and non-electron
populations.
items.documentation:
Pedestal thermal electron energy is the random kinetic energy stored by the
bulk thermal electron population within the plasma pedestal. It is an
extensive energy content, not a local energy density or an energy-transfer
rate.

For nonrelativistic thermal electrons, the defining pressure integral is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{ped},e} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_{\mathrm{ped}}} p_{e,\mathrm{th}}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{ped},e}$ is the pedestal thermal electron energy,
$V_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the volume occupied by the pedestal region,
$p_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the scalar thermal-electron pressure, and $dV$ is the
physical volume element. The scalar pressure is one-third of the trace of
the pressure tensor associated with random thermal-electron motion.

The integral covers only the pedestal region, rather than the entire
confined plasma, and excludes suprathermal electrons, directed bulk-flow
energy, and non-electron populations. Restricting the volume integral
defining [thermal electron energy](name:thermal_electron_energy) to the
pedestal gives this quantity. The corresponding energy stored by pedestal
ions is [pedestal thermal ion energy](name:pedestal_thermal_ion_energy).

items.name: runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer
items.description:
Runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation is the volumetric
rate at which parallel electric acceleration drives electrons from the
thermal distribution's suprathermal tail into runaway motion.
items.documentation:
Runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer generation is the volumetric
production rate of electrons entering the runaway population through Dreicer
acceleration. The electric-field component parallel to the magnetic field
drives suprathermal electrons across the critical velocity-space boundary
beyond which electric acceleration overcomes collisional friction.

The kinetic definition is the velocity-space flux across that critical
boundary into the runaway population:

$$
S_{\mathrm{D}} = \int_{\Sigma_c} \boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{D}}_v \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_v \, dA_v
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the runaway-electron source rate due to Dreicer
generation, $\Sigma_c$ is the critical boundary separating the collisional
and runaway regions of velocity space, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{D}}_v$
is the electron velocity-space flux associated with parallel electric
acceleration and collisional friction, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_v$ is the unit
normal pointing into the runaway region, and $dA_v$ is a surface element of
that boundary.

This quantity counts primary production from the thermal distribution's
tail. It excludes avalanche multiplication, [hot-tail
production](name:runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_hot_tail), and other
non-Dreicer sources. It is a source contribution to the runaway-electron
density balance, not the full density time derivative, which also includes
other sources, losses, and transport.

Spatial averaging preserves this population and mechanism scope: the
[volume-averaged Dreicer source
rate](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_dreicer) is
the volume-weighted plasma mean of this production term, not a
volume-integrated generation rate. The [fast-electron Dreicer source rate]
instead counts entry into the defined fast-electron population; the two
coincide only when that population is defined to coincide with the runaway
population.

items.name: hydrogen_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local particle number density of hydrogen ions in the boundary plasma
immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the
plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
items.documentation:
Hydrogen density at a limiter is the local number density of hydrogen ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance; neutral hydrogen is excluded. For hydrogen,
the charge-state sum reduces to the density of positively charged hydrogen
ions, H+.

The local hydrogen-ion density is defined from the velocity distribution
function:

$$
n_{\mathrm{H}^+} = \int f_{\mathrm{H}^+}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density,
$f_{\mathrm{H}^+}$ is the hydrogen-ion velocity distribution function, and
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity at the evaluation point.

This quantity is the hydrogen-specific component of
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter). It counts hydrogen ions
separately from
[deuterium_density_at_limiter](name:deuterium_density_at_limiter), and does
not include neutral hydrogen or other ion species.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of deuterium ions at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the deuterium-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local deuterium number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_D = \frac{dN_D}{dV}
$$

where $N_D$ is the number of deuterium ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the deuterium-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target and is summed over all positive atomic deuterium
ionization states, counting each ion once regardless of charge state.
Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules, electrons, and ions of other species
are excluded.

Unlike
[deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_divertor_target),
which includes both fuel-ion species, this quantity contains deuterium ions
only. It is the divertor-target-localized counterpart of
[deuterium_density](name:deuterium_density).

items.name: co_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from co-passing fast
particles to bulk thermal electrons, averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal-electron collisional power density is the signed rate of
kinetic-energy transfer from co-passing fast particles to bulk thermal
electrons, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. The orbit restriction
applies to the donating fast-particle distribution, not to the receiving
thermal electrons.

It is defined by the thermal-electron kinetic-energy moment of the
corresponding Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{e,co}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_{\mathrm e}|\mathbf v|^2 C_{\mathrm ea}[f_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{co}}] \, d^3v \right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{e,co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this collisional power density,
$m_{\mathrm e}$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf v$ is electron velocity, and
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The index $a$ runs over the
fast species represented by the donating distribution; $f_{\mathrm
e}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the bulk thermal-electron velocity distribution, and
$f_a^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the fast-species distribution restricted to
co-passing guiding-center orbits. The operator $C_{\mathrm ea}$ gives the
collisional rate of change of the thermal-electron distribution caused by
that fast-species contribution. Angle brackets denote the
volume-shell-weighted flux-surface average, and $\psi$ labels the averaging
surface.

This quantity is an energy source or sink, not stored thermal-electron
energy. It excludes energy transferred to ions or suprathermal electrons and
excludes the counter-passing and trapped parts of the donating distribution.

With the same flux-surface averaging applied to every term, this
contribution, the [counter-passing
contribution](name:counter_passing_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions),
and the [trapped
contribution](name:trapped_thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions)
sum to the orbit-unrestricted [thermal-electron collisional power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer net kinetic
energy from co-passing fast particles to bulk thermal electrons.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_source
items.description:
Toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the neutral
population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states. Its sign
distinguishes neutral momentum transfer along increasing versus decreasing
toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for the
neutral population in the edge plasma, summed over all neutral states, is
the net neutral momentum transfer per unit area resolved along the toroidal
direction. It is one component of the aggregate [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source) acting in the neutral momentum
balance.

The toroidal component is defined by projecting the parent source vector
onto the toroidal unit vector:

$$
S_{\phi,n} = \boldsymbol{S}_n \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $S_{\phi,n}$ is the toroidal neutral momentum source,
$\boldsymbol{S}_n$ is the area-normalized [neutral momentum
source](name:neutral_momentum_source) vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The quantity is summed over all neutral states and excludes ion momentum
sources. Unlike the [radial neutral momentum
source](name:radial_neutral_momentum_source), [poloidal neutral momentum
source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source), and [parallel neutral
momentum source](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_source), it resolves
momentum transfer along the toroidal direction rather than along major
radius, the local poloidal direction, or the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral momentum source points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: reference_major_radius
items.description:
Reference major radius is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis to the designated location at which the vacuum toroidal
magnetic field is specified.
items.documentation:
Reference major radius is the geometric [radius](name:radius) measured
perpendicularly from the toroidal symmetry axis to the designated location
where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is specified. It is a selected
reference value of [major radius](name:major_radius).

For an axisymmetric vacuum toroidal field, the reference radius and its
associated field value determine the inverse-major-radius dependence:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}(R)=B_0\frac{R_0}{R}
$$

where $R_0$ is the reference major radius, $B_0$ is the vacuum toroidal
magnetic-field component at that radius, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate,
and $B_{\phi,\mathrm{vac}}(R)$ is the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field
component at $R$. The right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame uses
toroidal angle $\phi$ and vertical coordinate $Z$.

The reference location is prescribed; it need not coincide with the magnetic
axis or the equatorial midplane. Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged major
radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_major_radius), this quantity is not an
average over a magnetic flux surface. The reference radius and associated
vacuum field provide the reference parameters used in toroidal-flux
coordinate definitions and current-density normalizations.

items.name: area_of_rogowski_coil
items.description:
Area of a Rogowski coil is the effective cross-sectional area linked by one
sensing turn of the closed winding. It is a geometric area factor; with
winding turn density it determines the ideal current-sensing sensitivity.
items.documentation:
Area of a Rogowski coil is the effective cross-sectional area linked by one
sensing turn of a closed Rogowski winding. It is a scalar geometry factor of
the winding, not the signed current threaded by the coil or the measured
coil voltage.

In the ideal uniformly wound limit, the area appears as the non-negative
sensitivity factor in the linear constitutive relation between coil voltage
and enclosed-current time derivative:

$$
V_R(t) = \sigma \mu_0 n A \frac{d I_\mathrm{enc}}{dt}
$$

where $A$ is the Rogowski-coil area, $n$ is the winding turn density along
the closed winding path, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability,
$I_\mathrm{enc}$ is the signed [Rogowski-coil
current](name:current_of_rogowski_coil) threaded by the coil, $V_R$ is the
Rogowski-coil voltage, and $\sigma$ is the sign set by winding orientation
and terminal polarity.

The effective area may represent a calibrated equivalent for a real winding
with finite pitch or nonuniform cross-section, but it remains a per-turn
area factor. It is in the same geometric-coil-area family as [area of a
poloidal magnetic field probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe)
and [area of a toroidal magnetic field
probe](name:area_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe); multiplying by turn
density, turn number, or path length gives related sensitivity factors, not
this quantity.

items.name: radial_velocity_of_pellet
items.description:
Signed major-radius component of the pellet center-of-mass velocity,
describing motion toward or away from the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed major-radius component of the translational
velocity of the pellet center of mass. It resolves motion in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The radial velocity is defined by:

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}} \cdot \hat{R} = \frac{dR_{\mathrm{cm}}}{dt}
$$

where $v_R$ is the radial velocity component, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is
the center-of-mass translational velocity vector, $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector toward increasing major radius, $R_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the
center-of-mass major-radius coordinate, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to the pellet center of mass. For fragment-resolved
motion, it applies to the individual fragment center of mass; for collective
fragment-cloud motion, it applies to the cloud center of mass at the shatter
cone origin. The cloud center of mass is mass-weighted, rather than an
equal-weight average of fragment positions, and its motion is distinct from
the spread of individual fragment velocities.

This component is not the total speed, a flux-surface-normal velocity, or
rotational motion about the represented center of mass. Together with the
[toroidal velocity](name:toroidal_velocity_of_pellet) and [vertical
velocity](name:vertical_velocity_of_pellet), it specifies the translational
velocity vector when all components refer to the same entity and instant.
For the pellet at vacuum-chamber entry, it is the radial component of the
[initial velocity](name:initial_velocity_of_pellet); the radial quantity
itself is not restricted to that instant.

Sign convention: Positive when the represented center of mass moves toward
increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: parallel_fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of fast ions of one species is their kinetic stress from random
motion along the magnetic field, summed over all charge states and excluding
thermal-ion contributions.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the field-parallel principal
component of their gyrotropic pressure tensor, summed over all charge
states. Together with the [perpendicular fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure), it characterizes the
species' anisotropic suprathermal stress relative to the local magnetic
field.

The parallel pressure is defined by the charge-state-summed second central
velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_c m_i \int \left[(\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{i,c})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right]^2 f_{i,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-ion pressure of
species $i$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $c$ labels ionic charge states, $m_i$
is the ion mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
$f_{i,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion number distribution in velocity
space for species $i$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{u}_{i,c}$ is that
distribution's mean velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ follows
the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

Only the suprathermal population of the specified ion species is included.
Contributions from all charge states are added directly, not
density-weighted; each contribution is a [charge-state-resolved parallel
fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_fast_ion_state_pressure). Thermal-ion
pressure, electron pressure, and directed bulk-flow momentum flux are
excluded. This component is neither the perpendicular pressure nor an
isotropic trace average.

Summing this quantity over ion species gives the [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), which is the
field-parallel component of the aggregate [fast-ion pressure
tensor](name:fast_ion_pressure).
