items.name: poloidal_electron_energy_flux
items.description:
Poloidal electron energy flux is the signed electron kinetic-energy flow per
unit area normal to the local poloidal direction around the magnetic axis.
items.documentation:
Poloidal electron energy flux represents local electron kinetic-energy
transport around the magnetic axis through a surface normal to the poloidal
direction. It includes conductive and particle-carried contributions to the
electron energy balance.

The component is defined by projection:

$$
\Gamma_{e,W,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,W,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electron energy flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{e,W}$ is the full [electron energy
flux](name:electron_energy_flux) vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$
is the local poloidal unit vector. The poloidal direction lies in a plane of
constant toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is upward vertical position.

This is a local directional component, not a poloidal integral, flux-surface
average, or integrated power. It excludes ion-carried energy, whose
corresponding component is [poloidal ion energy
flux](name:poloidal_ion_energy_flux). Unlike [poloidal electron particle
flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), it describes transported energy
rather than transported electron number.

Sign convention: Positive when electron energy flows clockwise around the
magnetic axis in a poloidal cross-section viewed with the toroidal symmetry
axis on the left and increasing $Z$ upward.

items.name: nitrogen_prefill_count
items.description:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂)
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 7 per atom or 14 per N₂ molecule.
items.documentation:
Nitrogen prefill count is the total amount of neutral nitrogen (N or N₂)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral nitrogen atom contributes 7
equivalent electrons, so each N₂ molecule contributes 14.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}} = 7N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}} + 14N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \left[7\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}(t) + 14\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}(t)\right]dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{N,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{N_2,prefill}}$ are
accumulated neutral atom and molecule counts, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N}}$ and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ are their introduction rates. The counts are pure
counts, the rates are in s$^{-1}$, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the
prefill start and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This quantity includes only neutral nitrogen introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the nitrogen component
of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), whereas accumulated_nitrogen_count
represents post-breakdown nitrogen accumulation.

items.name: verdet_constant_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Magneto-optic coefficient relating optical polarization rotation in a fiber
to the magnetic-field component along the optical propagation path.
items.documentation:
The Verdet constant is the material- and wavelength-dependent coefficient
governing Faraday rotation in an optical fiber. It characterizes the fiber's
intrinsic magneto-optic response for a specified material state and optical
wavelength.

For a uniform fiber segment, the Faraday rotation is defined by

$$
\theta_F = V B_{\parallel} L
$$

where $\theta_F$ is the Faraday polarization-rotation angle, $V$ is the
Verdet constant, $B_{\parallel}$ is the magnetic-field component along the
local optical propagation direction, and $L$ is the optical path length
through the fiber segment.

This quantity is a local fiber property, not the path-integrated
polarization rotation of a complete sensor. It applies to the optical fiber
material and state specified by the physical system and does not represent
the total magnetic-field magnitude or a field component transverse to the
propagation direction.

For a nonuniform fiber or magnetic field, the accumulated rotation is
obtained from the path integral of the local product $V B_{\parallel}$ along
the optical path; the [length of the fiber-optic current
sensor](name:length_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor) supplies the
corresponding total propagation distance but is not itself part of the
Verdet constant.

items.name: total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state, integrated
over the plasma and including both the toroidal projection of the
thermal-ion contribution and the summed fast-ion contributions from
angular-momentum exchange with co-existing species.
items.documentation:
Coulomb-collisional torque on ions in a specified charge state is the signed
toroidal collisional angular-momentum source for that charge state,
integrated over the plasma. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$
direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total torque is the additive thermal-plus-fast scalar contribution:

$$
\tau^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
=
\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}
+
\sum_f \tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $i$ identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies the charge state,
$\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is
the [thermal ion charge-state collisional
torque](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
$\hat{Z}\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{th}}_{i,q,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its
axial projection associated with toroidal angular momentum, $f$ indexes
fast-ion sub-populations, and
$\tau^{\mathrm{fast},\phi}_{i,q,f,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the [toroidal fast ion
charge-state collisional
torque](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions) for
sub-population $f$.

Only torque due to Coulomb-collisional momentum exchange with co-existing
charged plasma species is included. This quantity is charge-state resolved,
not summed over charge states, and is distinct from the corresponding local
total ion charge-state collisional torque density.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions transfer toroidal angular momentum
to the specified ion charge state in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: thermal_ion_energy
items.description:
Volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion ensemble over a
specified plasma region, excluding electron, fast-ion, and suprathermal
contributions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the internal energy stored by the thermal-ion ensemble
within a specified plasma volume. It aggregates the included thermal-ion
populations and excludes electron energy and nonthermal ion populations,
including fast and suprathermal ions.

For an isotropic thermal-ion pressure, the volume-integrated energy is
defined by

$$
E_{i,\mathrm{th}} = \int_V u_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV = \frac{3}{2}\int_V p_{i,\mathrm{th}}\,dV
$$

where $E_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion energy, $V$ is the selected
plasma volume, $u_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-ion internal-energy
density, $p_{i,\mathrm{th}}$ is the total isotropic thermal-ion pressure,
and $dV$ is the physical volume element.

The integration region is part of the concrete specialization: it may be
restricted to the H-mode pedestal, as in [pedestal thermal ion
energy](name:pedestal_thermal_ion_energy), or encompass the complete
thermal-ion ensemble, as in [total thermal ion
energy](name:total_thermal_ion_energy). The quantity is an aggregate over
the included thermal-ion populations rather than a single-ion or
charge-state-resolved energy.

This is the thermal-ion component of [ion energy](name:ion_energy). It
differs from total ion energy by excluding fast and suprathermal ion
contributions, and it differs from electron energy by including only thermal
ions.

items.name: plasma_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination or
neutralization of plasma ions at the plasma-material interface, summed over
all targets. It represents the plasma-ion surface recombination contribution
to the total divertor heat load.
items.documentation:
Plasma recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to
divertor target surfaces when plasma ions recombine or neutralize at the
plasma-material interface. It is the plasma-ion surface-deposition channel
of [total divertor recombination
power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), integrated over all
divertor targets.

It is defined as the surface integral of the local deposited-power density
over the divertor target assembly:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{plasma} = \int_{A_\mathrm{div}} q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma} \, dA
$$

where $A_\mathrm{div}$ is the union of all divertor target surfaces, $dA$ is
a target-surface element, and $q_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{plasma}$ is the local
non-negative deposited-power density due only to recombination or
neutralization of plasma ions incident from the plasma side.

This quantity is the plasma-component counterpart of
[power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).
The complementary neutral-particle channel is
[neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination);
conducted, convected, radiated, and other non-recombination heat-load
contributions are excluded. It may be equivalently represented as the sum of
[plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)
over the target surfaces included in $A_\mathrm{div}$.
